motivation: Understanding the spectra of few-lepton Coulomb systems, such as positronium molecules, is of fundamental interest in atomic physics.
method: They use an extended stochastic variational method combined with the complex scaling method to resolve natural-parity S- and P-wave spectra.
result: They find Gailitis–Damburg sequences near thresholds with inverse-square attraction, and different systems show varying resonance densities.
conclusion: The work provides comprehensive spectral data and reveals connections between molecular and atomic configurations in these exotic systems.

title: 6-valent Vertex In The $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ Web Category And Its Categorification
authors: Jernej Grlj, Mikhail Khovanov, Haihan Wu, Melissa Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21566v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define a [MATH]-rotationally invariant 6-valent vertex in the [MATH] web category. When [MATH], we provide a categorification of the 6-valent vertex using [MATH] foams and decompose the hexagon web into a direct sum of indecomposables. A similar decomposition is conjectured for [MATH].
tldr: This paper defines and categorifies a rotationally invariant 6-valent vertex in the gl_N web category using foams.
motivation: To understand the structure of web categories and provide categorifications that might lead to new invariants.
method: They define the vertex and categorify it using foam theory, then decompose the hexagon web into indecomposables.
result: They provide a categorification for a specific N (likely N=3) and conjecture a similar decomposition for other N.
conclusion: This work advances the categorification program for web categories.

title: Output Feedback Guaranteed Cost Equilibrium In Networked Multi-Agent Linear-Quadratic Difference Games
authors: Puduru Viswanadha Reddy Aniruddha Roy
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21568v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study infinite-horizon deterministic linear-quadratic difference games with an output feedback information structure. We consider linear time-invariant dynamics and quadratic cost functionals defined over an infinite horizon. We first demonstrate that computing an output feedback Nash equilibrium (OF-NE) in difference games is challenging, even for low-dimensional games. To address this difficulty, we introduce an output feedback guaranteed cost equilibrium (OF-GCE) for difference games. In an OF-GCE, each player seeks a feedback strategy that guarantees its cost remains below a prescribed bound while satisfying an equilibrium condition. We derive necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of an OF-GCE in terms of the solvability of a set of coupled bilinear matrix inequalities. We provide a linear matrix inequality-based iterative algorithm for synthesizing OF-GCE strategies. We further show that the state feedback GCE (SF-GCE) is a special case of the OF-GCE when players have complete state information. Numerical examples illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.
tldr: 该论文研究网络化多智能体线性二次差分博弈中的输出反馈保证成本均衡，提出基于线性矩阵不等式的求解算法。
motivation: 输出反馈纳什均衡在差分博弈中难以计算，需要引入保证成本均衡以简化问题。
method: 通过耦合的双线性矩阵不等式描述存在条件，并设计迭代算法求解线性矩阵不等式。
result: 推导出输出反馈保证成本均衡存在的充要条件，并证明状态反馈是输出反馈的特例。
conclusion: 为网络化多智能体博弈提供了一种可行的输出反馈均衡求解方法。

title: Open-Loop Riemannian Frank--Wolfe: Fast Rates Under Error Bounds And Scaling Inequalities
authors: Kangming Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We explore fast convergence of the Riemannian Frank--Wolfe method for smooth geodesically convex optimization over compact feasible sets. Hadamard manifolds are the main setting. On general complete manifolds, the analysis accounts for all feasible minimizing geodesics. We consider the open loop step-size [MATH], which only uses the iteration index. Under a local H\"olderian error bound and local length-normalized directional scaling, every [MATH] gives the eventual rate [MATH] for [MATH]. An interior-ball condition yields [MATH] for strongly geodesically convex objectives. Under an exact Riemannian scaling inequality and a uniform positive lower bound on the gradient norm, every [MATH] gives [MATH] after an explicit threshold index. The same rate holds for the smallest Frank--Wolfe gap over the most recent half of the iterates. For geodesic balls of radius \(R<\pi/2\) in the unit sphere, we establish the scaling inequality with [MATH], yielding [MATH] primal error and recent-window gap rates. We also analyze the standard gap-feedback short step under the local error-bound conditions, obtaining [MATH] for [MATH] and a linear rate for [MATH]. Numerical experiments illustrate the predicted rates and compare iteration-only and feedback-based step selection.
tldr: This paper analyzes convergence rates of the Riemannian Frank-Wolfe method for geodesically convex optimization under error bounds and scaling inequalities.
motivation: To establish fast convergence rates for Frank-Wolfe on manifolds using only iteration-dependent step sizes, improving upon existing results.
method: The authors consider open-loop step sizes and analyze convergence under local Hölderian error bounds and directional scaling conditions, also studying gap-feedback step sizes.
result: They derive explicit rates (e.g., O(1/k)) for general manifolds and linear convergence for strongly geodesically convex objectives under an interior-ball condition, with experiments validating the theory.
conclusion: The paper provides a comprehensive rate analysis for Riemannian Frank-Wolfe, but it is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Revenue And Social Welfare Maximization In Service Systems: Independent Vs Grouped Customers
authors: Antonis Economou Apostolos Burnetas
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21608v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The revenue maximization problem in service systems with strategic customers is a central problem in the thread of Rational Queueing literature. The standard modeling assumption is that customers act independently and, therefore, the situation is modeled as a game among the customers and the service provider. In the present work, we focus on the case where the customers are grouped and controlled by their leader and the situation becomes a game between the customers' leader and the service provider. We examine the effect of customers' cooperation for the join-or-balk dilemma at the unobservable single-server Markovian queue and present the impact on the social welfare and service provider's revenue.
tldr: This paper analyzes revenue and social welfare in service systems with strategic customers, comparing independent decision-making versus grouped decision-making in a Markovian queue.
motivation: To understand how customer cooperation affects the join-or-balk dilemma and the resulting revenue for the service provider and social welfare.
method: The authors model the situation as a game between customers (either independent or grouped with a leader) and the service provider, using a single-server Markovian queue with unobservable queue length.
result: The paper presents the impact of customer grouping on the equilibrium behavior, revenue, and social welfare compared to the independent case.
conclusion: The study provides insights into how cooperation among customers influences optimal pricing and welfare outcomes in service systems.

title: Effective Uniqueness Of The Measure Of Maximal Entropy In Ornstein's $\bar{d}$-metric
authors: Teena Kumari Vaughn Climenhaga
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21703v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Every topologically mixing shift of finite type has a unique measure of maximal entropy. It follows from Ornstein theory that every invariant measure with entropy close to maximal must be close to the MME in the [MATH]-metric. We prove a quantitative version of this, strengthening earlier results of Kadyrov that established effective uniqueness in the Wasserstein metric.
tldr: The paper proves a quantitative version of the uniqueness of the measure of maximal entropy for shifts of finite type in the d-bar metric.
motivation: To strengthen earlier results of Kadyrov that established effective uniqueness in the Wasserstein metric, providing a quantitative bound in Ornstein's metric.
method: Uses Ornstein theory and properties of shifts of finite type to derive an effective bound on the distance between any invariant measure with entropy close to maximal and the MME in the d-bar metric.
result: Obtains an explicit quantitative estimate for the closeness in the d-bar metric, improving on prior work.
conclusion: The result provides a refined understanding of convergence to the measure of maximal entropy in symbolic dynamics.

title: Tensor Greedy Double Block Extended Kaczmarz Method For Solving Inconsistent Tensor Linear Systems Under T-product
authors: Lionel Tondji J\'er\'emie Mabiala
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21705v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The randomized extended Kaczmarz method is an effective iterative framework for solving large-scale inconsistent linear systems. In this paper, we extend this framework to third-order inconsistent tensor linear systems under the t-product and propose the Tensor Greedy Double Block Extended Kaczmarz (TGDBEK) method. At each iteration, TGDBEK dynamically constructs active blocks of row and column slices via a residual-based greedy selection strategy, prioritizing the slices associated with the largest residual norms. Unlike existing tensor block Kaczmarz variants that rely on static, predefined partitions -- the tensor randomized extended block Kaczmarz (TREBK) method, its greedy counterpart (TREGBK), and the tensor randomized extended average block Kaczmarz (TREABK) method -- TGDBEK adapts the active block sizes dynamically at each step using a single intuitive threshold parameter [MATH]. We establish the theoretical linear convergence of TGDBEK to the unique minimum-norm least-squares solution [MATH]. Extensive numerical benchmarks on synthetic dense and sparse tensor systems, as well as multidimensional multichannel color and 3D volumetric MRI image deblurring problems, demonstrate that TGDBEK substantially outperforms state-of-the-art tensor Kaczmarz solvers in both iteration count and CPU running time.
tldr: This paper proposes a new iterative method called Tensor Greedy Double Block Extended Kaczmarz (TGDBEK) for solving inconsistent tensor linear systems under the t-product, which dynamically selects active blocks based on residuals and demonstrates improved performance over existing methods.
motivation: The randomized extended Kaczmarz method is effective for large-scale inconsistent linear systems, and the authors aim to extend this framework to third-order tensor linear systems under the t-product, which arise in applications like image deblurring.
method: TGDBEK extends the extended Kaczmarz method to tensors by using a residual-based greedy selection strategy to dynamically construct active blocks of row and column slices, with block sizes adapted via a single threshold parameter at each iteration.
result: The paper establishes linear convergence of TGDBEK to the unique minimum-norm least-squares solution and shows through numerical benchmarks on synthetic and real data (color and 3D MRI image deblurring) that it substantially outperforms state-of-the-art tensor Kaczmarz solvers in iteration count and CPU time.
conclusion: The proposed method is an efficient and effective solver for inconsistent tensor linear systems, particularly well-suited for multidimensional image deblurring problems.

title: $q$-Berezin Sectorial Operators With Applications To $q$-Berezin Number Inequalities And $q$-Berezin Ranges
authors: Saikat Mahapatra, Subhadip Halder, Riddhick Birbonshi, Arnab Patra, Kallol Paul
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21723v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new class of operators, called [MATH]-Berezin sectorial operators, as an extension of the class of [MATH]-sectorial operators. By presenting examples on the Hardy-Hilbert space, we show that there exist operators which are [MATH]-Berezin sectorial but not [MATH]-sectorial. Several new inequalities for the [MATH]-Berezin number associated with this class of operators are also derived. In addition, we investigate the geometric structure of the [MATH]-Berezin range for various classes of operators on the Bergman space, including weighted shift and certain composition operators.
tldr: The paper introduces q-Berezin sectorial operators as an extension of q-sectorial operators, derives new inequalities for the q-Berezin number, and studies the geometry of the q-Berezin range on Bergman spaces.
motivation: To generalize sectorial operators using q-calculus and investigate their properties, potentially leading to new insights in operator theory.
method: Define q-Berezin sectorial operators, provide examples on Hardy-Hilbert space, derive inequalities for the q-Berezin number, and analyze the q-Berezin range for weighted shift and composition operators on Bergman space.
result: Demonstrates that q-Berezin sectorial operators generalize q-sectorial operators, obtains new inequalities, and characterizes geometric structures of the q-Berezin range for specific operator classes.
conclusion: Establishes a new class of operators with foundational results, opening avenues for further research in operator theory and q-calculus.

title: Construction And Design Of Mpac Codes
authors: Fangbo Yi, Zuoxin Cai, Zhongjun Yang, Li Chen, Huazi Zhang, Wenxin Liu, Yuan Li
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21757v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes modified polarization-adjusted convolutional (MPAC) codes and their hybrid decoding that achieves an improved performance-complexity tradeoff. For MPAC codes, only a subset of the information bits undergo the convolutional transform. The output is then combined with the remaining information bits for the inner polar transform. Correspondingly, the convolutionally transformed bits are recovered by Fano decoding, while the remaining information bits are recovered by the successive cancellation (SC) decoding, constituting the hybrid Fano-successive cancellation (HFSC) decoding. The MPAC codes are further designed by the coset-wise analysis that characterizes the number of minimum weight codewords (MWCs). It is discovered that a partially convolutional transform can improve the codeword through utilizing the row combinations of the frozen set efficiently. This property enables the MPAC codes to outperform their prototype polarization-adjusted convolutional (PAC) codes and cyclic redundancy check (CRC)-polar codes. Furthermore, MPAC codes can be optimized by reducing the number of MWCs. Our numerical results demonstrate that, with a similar decoding complexity budget, the MPAC codes offer competent decoding performance when compared with PAC codes using Fano decoding and CRC-polar codes using SC list (SCL) decoding.
tldr: This paper introduces modified polarization-adjusted convolutional (MPAC) codes and a hybrid decoding scheme to improve the performance-complexity tradeoff of error-correcting codes.
motivation: The authors aim to enhance the performance of PAC codes and CRC-polar codes while maintaining manageable decoding complexity.
method: They propose MPAC codes where only a subset of information bits undergo a convolutional transform, and use a hybrid Fano and successive cancellation (HFSC) decoding strategy. The design is optimized via coset-wise analysis to reduce the number of minimum weight codewords.
result: Numerical results show that MPAC codes with similar decoding complexity achieve competitive performance compared to PAC and CRC-polar codes.
conclusion: MPAC codes offer a promising alternative in channel coding, but the work is purely classical coding theory without quantum information or thermodynamic connection.

title: Virtual Element Approximations For Distributed Or Neumann Boundary Optimal Control Problems Governed By Poroelasticity Equation
authors: Thirupathi Gudi, David Mora, Nitesh Verma
abstract: ArXiv:2608.22107v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigate the conforming virtual element method for the optimal control problem governed by the linear poroelasticity equation. Both distributed control and Neumann boundary controls are considered with the optimize-then-discretize approach. We establish the well-posedness of the discrete state and adjoint problems in three-field formulation by deriving the first-order optimality condition. The optimal a priori error estimates are developed through a novel poroelastic projection for both control problems, and these estimates are uniform with respect to the relevant physical parameters of the model problem. Moreover, the numerical experiments are carried out using the primal dual active set strategy, and demonstrate the support for the derived theoretical results.
tldr: This paper develops conforming virtual element methods for optimal control problems governed by poroelasticity, covering both distributed and Neumann boundary controls.
motivation: To solve optimal control problems for poroelasticity equations using a reliable numerical method with optimal error estimates.
method: Conforming virtual element method with optimize-then-discretize approach, deriving first-order optimality conditions and a priori error estimates via a novel poroelastic projection, with numerical experiments using primal dual active set strategy.
result: Optimal a priori error estimates uniform with respect to physical parameters are established, and numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results.
conclusion: The proposed virtual element method offers an accurate and efficient numerical approach for the considered poroelasticity optimal control problems.

title: Log-H\"oder Continuity At Zero Lyapunov Gap For Finite State Markov $GL(2)$-cocycles
authors: El Hadji Yaya Tall
abstract: ArXiv:2608.22157v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the extremal Lyapunov exponents of finite-state Markov [MATH]-cocycles are pointwise log-H\"older continuous, jointly in the cocycle matrices and the transition kernel, at every parameter [MATH] satisfying [MATH]. Perturbations are taken within a fixed transition graph. The main new ingredient is a Markov perpetuity estimate for the nonsplit triangular case, obtained through a martingale--coboundary decomposition. In the conformal case, the exponent [MATH] in the logarithmic modulus can be replaced by [MATH].
tldr: Proves log-Hölder continuity of extremal Lyapunov exponents for finite-state Markov GL(2)-cocycles at parameters with zero Lyapunov gap.
motivation: To establish regularity properties of Lyapunov exponents in ergodic theory, extending known results to the zero gap case.
method: Uses a Markov perpetuity estimate for the nonsplit triangular case and a martingale-coboundary decomposition.
result: Shows pointwise log-Hölder continuity jointly in the cocycle matrices and transition kernel, with an improved exponent in the conformal case.
conclusion: Provides a general continuity result for Lyapunov exponents in the context of Markov cocycles, contributing to dynamical systems theory.

title: A Counterexample To Universal Character Density For Compact Quantum Groups
authors: Zongjian Han
abstract: ArXiv:2608.22203v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1987, Woronowicz asked whether the linear span of irreducible characters is norm dense in the cocommutative part of the ambient C-star algebra of a compact quantum group. After thirty-nine calendar years, we give a negative answer to the universal form of this question, even for compact matrix quantum groups of Kac type. Starting from an infinite finitely generated simple group with property T and a finite bicharacter twist, we construct a compact quantum group whose universal C-star algebra is a full group C-star algebra. A Kazhdan projection is shown to remain cocommutative under the twisted coproduct, while a vector state arising from an induced representation separates this projection from every algebraic cocommutative element. Quantitatively, the distance from the Kazhdan projection to the closed linear span of irreducible characters is at least one half. Moreover, the projection lies in the kernel of the reducing morphism. The obstruction is therefore genuinely universal and disappears after passage to the reduced compact quantum group, where the known character-density theorem remains valid. The construction identifies a sharp boundary between universal and reduced character theory and shows that Kac symmetry alone does not control cocommutative elements in the universal completion.
tldr: This paper provides a counterexample to Woronowicz's 1987 question about character density in compact quantum groups, showing the universal version fails even for Kac-type compact matrix quantum groups.
motivation: Woronowicz had asked whether irreducible characters are norm dense in the cocommutative part of the universal C*-algebra of a compact quantum group; this question remained open for decades.
method: The author constructs a compact quantum group from an infinite finitely generated simple group with property T and a finite bicharacter twist, so that the universal C*-algebra is a full group C*-algebra. A Kazhdan projection is shown to be cocommutative but not approximable by algebraic cocommutative elements.
result: The distance from the Kazhdan projection to the closed linear span of irreducible characters is at least 1/2, and the projection lies in the kernel of the reducing morphism, showing the obstruction is universal and vanishes in the reduced completion.
conclusion: The construction reveals a sharp boundary between universal and reduced character theory, indicating that Kac symmetry does not ensure density in the universal setting.

title: On Convergence Behavior Of Randomized Kaczmarz-type Methods For Solving Doubly Noisy Linear Systems
authors: Gang Wu Yudan Gan
abstract: ArXiv:2608.22259v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The randomized Kaczmarz (RK) method is an efficient iterative projection algorithm with low computational complexity for solving consistent linear systems. However, noise is inevitable in real-world applications, and both the coefficient matrix and the right-hand side vector may be contaminated by noise. The convergence analysis of RK-type methods for doubly noisy linear systems, where both the system matrix and the measurement vector are perturbed, remains relatively limited. In this paper, we investigate the limiting behavior of the RK algorithm for solving doubly noisy inconsistent linear systems without imposing any additional initial assumptions. Furthermore, to the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first convergence analysis of the randomized extended Kaczmarz (REK), randomized block Kaczmarz (RBK), and randomized double block Kaczmarz (RDBK) algorithms for doubly noisy linear systems. We prove that these algorithms converge to a neighborhood of the least-squares solution of the underlying noiseless system. Compared with existing theoretical estimates, the proposed bounds effectively characterize the convergence behavior of these algorithms when applied to doubly noisy linear systems. Finally, numerical experiments are conducted to validate the theoretical results.
tldr: This paper analyzes the convergence behavior of randomized Kaczmarz-type algorithms for solving doubly noisy linear systems, providing theoretical bounds and numerical validation.
motivation: Real-world linear systems often have noise in both the coefficient matrix and the measurement vector, and the convergence of randomized Kaczmarz methods under such doubly noisy conditions is not well understood.
method: The paper studies the limiting behavior of the randomized Kaczmarz (RK) algorithm and provides the first convergence analysis for randomized extended Kaczmarz (REK), randomized block Kaczmarz (RBK), and randomized double block Kaczmarz (RDBK) algorithms in the doubly noisy setting.
result: It proves that these algorithms converge to a neighborhood of the least-squares solution of the underlying noiseless system, and the proposed bounds characterize the convergence better than existing ones.
conclusion: The work fills a gap in theoretical understanding of RK-type methods under doubly noisy perturbations, supported by numerical experiments.

title: A Case-Control Measurement Study Of Osint Source Effectiveness For Critical Infrastructure Defense
authors: Ekrem E. Emeksiz, Jeel Piyushkumar Khatiwala, Divyangkumar Patel, Weifeng Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Defenders of critical infrastructure (CI) subscribe to many public open-source intelligence (OSINT) feeds without an empirical basis for which feeds actually precede attacks. We provide one. Across 54 confirmed CI cyberattacks from 2010 through 2024 spanning twelve named CI sectors plus a cross-sector category (consolidation rules in Section IV), paired with 12 null-control vulnerability cases drawn from the same source space, we audit per-source attack coverage, null-case contamination, and signal lead time for ten public OSINT source classes that meet a minimum-volume threshold. Sources separate cleanly into three operationally distinct mission profiles (pooled Fisher exact p = 3.4x10^-8): precursor (six classes with zero observed null firings at coverage at or above 5%), disclosure-exposure (three classes whose null contamination meets or exceeds attack coverage), and one large broad-coverage class that mixes the two profiles but retains 91.3% within-corpus precision. The precision-side classification is stable across a 2019 temporal partition and across a US-versus-non-US geographic partition. Two sources, one broad-coverage and one precursor, cover 92.6% of corpus attacks; three cover 96.3%. The greedy portfolio at k = 3 outperforms the mean random three-source subset by 39.8 percentage points. Several source classes widely treated as canonical for industrial control system defense fall into the disclosure-exposure profile by operational mission, not by quality. Per-sector, per-actor, and per-jurisdiction portfolios diverge in rank order despite a shared rank-one source. The corpus, linkage protocol, and classification rules are released.
tldr: This paper presents an empirical study of open-source intelligence (OSINT) feed effectiveness for critical infrastructure cyber defense, using case-control analysis of 54 attacks.
motivation: Defenders lack empirical evidence on which OSINT sources actually precede attacks, so this study aims to provide a data-driven audit of source coverage and lead time.
method: The authors pair 54 confirmed CI cyberattacks with 12 null-control cases, audit ten OSINT source classes for attack coverage, null contamination, and signal lead time, and use statistical tests (Fisher exact) and temporal/geographic partitions for validation.
result: Sources separate into three mission profiles (precursor, disclosure-exposure, broad-coverage) with a greedy portfolio of three sources covering 96.3% of attacks, outperforming random subsets by 39.8 points.
conclusion: OSINT sources have distinct operational roles, and portfolio selection should be data-driven; the findings help prioritize feeds for CI defense.

title: SecOPD: Mitigating Adaptive Prompt Injections By On-Policy Distillation
authors: Yibo Peng, Long Lian, David Wagner, Sizhe Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21500v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Prompt injection is listed as the \#1 threat to AI agents. When an agent accesses external data from websites, files, or emails, an attacker may inject a prompt into the data, saying, "Ignore all prior instructions and perform ." To prevent arbitrary manipulation of agents, defenders try to train secure LLMs, which, however, still suffer from near 100% attack success rates (ASRs) against adaptive prompt injections. We note that this is because existing defensive finetuning recipes rely on sequence-level feedback signals (in DPO or GRPO). Treating an entire output equally prevents the model from learning precisely which output tokens are insecure. In this paper, we propose Secure On-Policy Distillation (SecOPD) that provides token-level feedback to guide defensive fine-tuning. The LLM receives an injected sample and produces a rollout, whose tokens are scored by the initialization model given the corresponding clean input. With more fine-grained training signals, our defended Qwen3.6-27B achieves a 9.0% ASR against the SoTA PISmith adaptive prompt injections, compared to 94.0% for the prior SoTA, Meta-SecAlign. The obtained security generalizes to domains completely unseen in training: in agentic tool calling, SecOPD achieves a 4.7% ASR compared to 5.5% for Meta-SecAlign. Code and the model are available at [URL] and [URL].
tldr: SecOPD defends LLMs against adaptive prompt injections by using token-level feedback in on-policy distillation, significantly reducing attack success rates.
motivation: Adaptive prompt injections pose a major threat to AI agents, with existing defensive fine-tuning methods like DPO or GRPO using sequence-level feedback, which fails to pinpoint insecure tokens.
method: SecOPD provides token-level feedback during fine-tuning by scoring each rollout token with the initialization model given the clean input, enabling more precise defensive training.
result: SecOPD achieves 9.0% attack success rate against SoTA adaptive attacks on Qwen3.6-27B, compared to 94.0% for Meta-SecAlign, and generalizes to unseen domains.
conclusion: Token-level feedback improves defensive fine-tuning against adaptive prompt injections, offering a more robust approach for securing LLM agents.

title: Cross-Layer Roots Of Trust: Integrating Biometrics, PUFs, And Hardware Obfuscation
authors: Nima Karimian
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21643v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern cyber--physical, Internet-of-Things (IoT), wearable, and edge systems increasingly require trust in three distinct entities: the human requesting access, the physical device executing the computation, and the hardware function that is permitted to operate. These requirements are usually studied in separate communities. Biometrics establish human identity but remain vulnerable to presentation attacks, intra-user variability, template leakage, and limited revocability. Physical unclonable functions (PUFs) provide device-specific physical identity and on-demand secret derivation, yet must address environmental instability, helper-data exposure, side channels, and modeling attacks. Hardware obfuscation and logic locking condition correct circuit behavior on an activation secret, but face oracle-guided, approximate, structural, removal, and physical attacks. This survey develops a unified human--device--function view of trust. We first decompose each primitive into its complete processing chain and identify the corresponding security assumptions, implementation mechanisms, and evaluation metrics. We then formalize pairwise compositions---biometric--PUF, PUF--obfuscation, and biometric--obfuscation---and a three-way architecture in which correct functionality is bound jointly to an authorized user and a genuine device. Particular attention is given to biometric key reconstruction, PUF stabilization and modeling resistance, logic-locking attack evaluation, cross-layer error propagation, enrollment trust, key lifecycle, and interface leakage. The survey concludes with a taxonomy and research agenda for revocable human--device credentials, compositional security, leakage-aware integration, reconfigurable activation, and standardized end-to-end evaluation.
tldr: This survey integrates biometrics, PUFs, and hardware obfuscation for cross-layer trust in human-device-function systems.
motivation: Modern cyber-physical systems require trust in multiple entities (human, device, function), but these are typically studied separately.
method: The survey decomposes each primitive, formalizes pairwise compositions, and proposes a three-way architecture binding functionality to authorized user and genuine device.
result: Provides a taxonomy and research agenda for revocable human-device credentials, compositional security, and leakage-aware integration.
conclusion: The paper highlights the need for unified trust frameworks across biometrics, PUFs, and hardware obfuscation.

title: Target-Dependent Local Verification: Information--Proof-Length Tradeoffs
authors: Hongmin Li

title: Ai Grinding For Fun And Cryptanalysis
authors: Bartosz Naskrecki Lukasz Olejnik
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21986v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an autonomous cryptanalysis workflow in which agents generate, test, and refine hypotheses before human review. The autonomous stage returns reproducible candidates with exact witnesses, controls, code, and run records. A researcher then decides whether the evidence establishes a break, defect, or coverage gap. Two failure modes recur. First, a public algebraic map or input representation erases or exposes a relation that a construction must hide. Examples include multiplication by zero, boundary coefficients of a polynomial product, quotients, characters, Schur squares, and variable-length byte encodings without boundaries. Second, a simulator, error law, or parameter certification uses a distribution different from the one claimed. Several targets fail in both ways. Every result has an exact witness and a discriminating control; every stated boundary has a proof. Three further targets yielded no attack but support narrower guarantees than a generic reading suggests. Eight published constructions fail at stated parameters or claims. A Ring-LWR commitment opens to every message with probability one. One ciphertext reveals two middle-product encryption rows. A lattice e-voting protocol loses receipt-freeness. A permutation-recovery attack against updatable encryption extends by linear algebra to the old decryption key. An explicit normal basis splits a degree-63 instance into seven degree-nine instances. A signature hash outside the lattice setting maps two printable equal-length messages to the same digest. A rerandomisable scheme's accept bit is a threshold oracle on its decryption noise. Separately, a group-ring decision claim and a multivariate MinRank hardening fail at the assumption or accounting level rather than as complete construction breaks. Each failure occurs one level above its supporting assumption.
tldr: An autonomous cryptanalysis workflow that uncovers failures in multiple cryptographic constructions through generated hypotheses and exact witnesses.
motivation: To automate the process of finding cryptographic weaknesses and to provide reproducible evidence for attacks.
method: Agents autonomously generate, test, and refine hypotheses, returning reproducible candidates with exact witnesses, controls, and run records for human review.
result: Eight published constructions fail at stated parameters; specific attacks include a Ring-LWR commitment that opens with probability one, ciphertext leaks, receipt-freeness loss, and more.
conclusion: The workflow exposes common failure modes in cryptographic designs and can validate coverage gaps, with every result supported by exact witnesses.

title: Norm-Query Complexity Of Algorithmic Problems In Finite-Dimensional P-adic Normed Spaces
authors: Huawei Wu Zhefan Duan
abstract: ArXiv:2608.22084v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the deterministic norm-query complexity of computational problems in finite-dimensional vector spaces over [MATH] equipped with an arbitrary ultrametric norm. For orthogonalization, we prove that no uniform finite query bound depending only on the dimension exists: for every deterministic algorithm that produces an [MATH]-orthogonal basis for every ultrametric norm [MATH], the number of norm queries is unbounded as [MATH] varies. We then study the Longest Vector Problem (LVP) for a rank-[MATH] [MATH]-adic lattice. By adapting a brute-force search to the general norm-query setting and eliminating the scalar redundancy among nonzero coefficient vectors modulo [MATH], we obtain an algorithm using exactly [MATH] norm queries for [MATH], and prove that no deterministic norm-query algorithm can use fewer queries in the worst case. Finally, we consider the Closest Vector Problem (CVP). Apart from the trivial cases in which no norm query is needed, we prove that the deterministic worst-case norm-query complexity of the CVP is unbounded, even when the lattice and the target vector are fixed.
tldr: This paper analyzes the deterministic norm-query complexity of algorithmic problems in finite-dimensional p-adic normed spaces, establishing unbounded query requirements for orthogonalization and closest vector problem, and an optimal finite bound for longest vector problem.
motivation: To understand the inherent computational difficulty of solving algebraic problems in p-adic vector spaces when only norm queries are allowed, which is a fundamental question in computational mathematics.
method: The authors study the query complexity by constructing algorithms and lower bounds for orthogonalization, longest vector problem, and closest vector problem under arbitrary ultrametric norms, using brute-force search and scalar redundancy elimination.
result: They prove that no uniform finite query bound exists for orthogonalization, the LVP has an exact query count for each dimension, and the CVP has unbounded query complexity even for fixed instances.
conclusion: The paper provides tight characterizations of query complexity for these problems, showing that some problems are not solvable with finite queries in the worst case.

title: A Lightweight And Post-Quantum Secure Framework For Iec 61869-9 Sampled Value Communication
authors: S. M. Suhail Hussain, Arman Ahmad, Mohammad Tayyab, Shaik Mullapathi Farooq
abstract: ArXiv:2608.22123v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Securing IEC 61869-9 Sampled Values (SV) is challenging because process-bus communication must satisfy stringent real-time constraints while supporting standardized high-rate publication profiles. This paper presents an experimentally validated security framework that combines lightweight per-frame authentication for operational SV traffic with post-quantum-capable key establishment protocol. For message integrity, the proposed method applies field-selective authentication employing optimized Chaskey-12 to reduce per-packet computational overhead. For trust establishment, the paper introduces an ML-KEM-based pairwise authentication and key-establishment procedure. The pairwise protocol is analyzed in the Quantum Random Oracle Model and is also verified with AVISPA tool under the Dolev-Yao adversarial model. A C-based publisher/subscriber prototype is implemented on a two-node process-bus testbed. Performance is evaluated across the eight IEC 61869-9 SV packet profiles using HMAC-256, AES-GMAC-128, Blake-2s, Chaskey-12, and a compiler-optimized Chaskey-12 implementations. These results indicate that optimized Chaskey-12 achieves ~90% lower latency than HMAC on SV packets. The proposed security framework is a practical and scalable candidate for protecting IEC 61869-9 SV traffic on resource-constrained digital-substation devices.
tldr: This paper proposes a lightweight security framework for IEC 61869-9 Sampled Value communication in digital substations, combining Chaskey-12 for per-frame authentication and ML-KEM for post-quantum key establishment.
motivation: Securing Sampled Value (SV) traffic in digital substations is challenging due to strict real-time constraints and the need for post-quantum security, while existing cryptographic solutions are too heavy for resource-constrained devices.
method: The authors introduce a field-selective authentication scheme using an optimized Chaskey-12 algorithm and a pairwise key establishment protocol based on ML-KEM, analyzing security in the Quantum Random Oracle Model and with the AVISPA tool.
result: Experimental evaluation on a two-node process-bus testbed across eight SV packet profiles shows that optimized Chaskey-12 achieves about 90% lower latency compared to HMAC, demonstrating practical feasibility.
conclusion: The proposed framework is a practical and scalable solution for protecting IEC 61869-9 SV traffic, addressing both real-time performance and post-quantum security requirements.

title: On SSI-based Private Decentralized Bidding
authors: Andreea Elena Dr\u{a}gnoiu, Nicoleta Dumitru, Ruxandra F. Olimid
abstract: ArXiv:2608.22525v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Private bidding is a process in which participants submit sealed bids, ensuring that their content remains hidden from other bidders during the bidding window. This is essential in competitive environments to ensure a fair and independent evaluation of all proposals. While (public) blockchain enables decentralized bidding and its transparency offers advantages such as public verifiability, without a Trusted Third Party (TTP), current methods struggle to verify whether a bidder is eligible. We propose a framework that leverages Self-Sovereign Identity (SSI) to address these issues by certifying the bid's eligibility and authenticity using the now-established SSI framework. To allow participants to prove they meet the requirements while keeping their bids secret, our model uses Verifiable Credentials (VCs) and cryptographic primitives such as Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs).
tldr: Proposes a framework using Self-Sovereign Identity and Zero-Knowledge Proofs for private decentralized bidding on blockchain.
motivation: Private bidding on public blockchain faces challenges in verifying eligibility without a trusted third party, as bids must remain secret.
method: Uses Verifiable Credentials and Zero-Knowledge Proofs to allow bidders to prove eligibility while keeping bids confidential.
result: The framework enables certification of bid eligibility and authenticity using established SSI and cryptographic primitives.
conclusion: The approach addresses the issue of private and verifiable bidding in decentralized environments.

title: Tight Weighted Second-Order Asymptotics For The Wyner--Ahlswede--K\"orner Problem Under Regular Posterior Geometry
authors: Daming Cao
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21991v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper determines the exact weighted normal approximation for the finite-alphabet Wyner--Ahlswede--K\"orner problem under local regularity of the posterior optimization. Liu's type-based achievability is governed by the variance of the weighted optimizer information density, whereas the known converse dispersion bound retains only the variance of its conditional expectation given the source pair. We show that the missing conditional-variance term is a genuine fixed-composition fluctuation. The converse first represents the auxiliary-variable optimization as a convexification problem on the posterior simplex and uses the associated dual deficit to quantify the suboptimality of code-induced posteriors. After conditioning on a joint type, a random deletion process yields an exact likelihood decomposition into a support-function score, a nonnegative predictable deficit, and a martingale. Posterior localization and barycentric inversion identify the martingale's predictable variance, while a variance-completion construction permits a martingale central limit theorem without conditioning on a terminal event. Averaging the fixed-type Gaussian bound over empirical joint types gives a total dispersion equal to the achievability variance. The uniqueness requirement is further relaxed to a variance-identifiability condition over all optimal posterior decompositions. A binary symmetric specialization verifies the assumptions and gives a closed form.
tldr: This paper derives exact weighted second-order asymptotics for the Wyner-Ahlswede-Körner problem under local regularity, closing the gap by including a conditional variance term.
motivation: The finite blocklength dispersion for the WAK problem was not fully characterized due to a missing conditional variance term in the converse. The authors aimed to tighten the second-order approximation to match achievability.
method: They use type-based achievability (Liu's method) and convexification on the posterior simplex, combined with a random deletion process and martingale central limit theorems to identify the conditional variance contribution.
result: They show that the total dispersion equals the achievability variance, prove a martingale CLT without terminal conditioning, and relax uniqueness to a variance-identifiability condition. A binary symmetric case yields a closed form.
conclusion: The paper provides a tight second-order characterization for the WAK problem under regular posterior geometry, resolving the dispersion gap.

title: Key Recovery From Residue-Confined Errors In Pradhan Crt-rlwe
authors: Bartosz Naskrecki Lukasz Olejnik
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21989v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the CRT-FHE scheme of Pradhan et al.\ is insecure for laws within its assumed error distribution range. The secret key follows from the public key by a single ring inversion whenever the public multiplier is a unit. The plaintext is recovered from any ciphertext under such a law without the secret key, for every multiplier, giving chosen-plaintext advantage [MATH]. We further show that the transformation from ordinary Ring-LWE to CRT-RLWE does not preserve the error distribution, so it does not establish that CRT-RLWE is at least as hard as Ring-LWE. One mechanism underlies both. The Chinese remainder theorem (CRT) function is reduced modulo [MATH] while its output is used modulo a coprime modulus [MATH], so under every zero-preserving section an error in [MATH] encodes to zero. The law [MATH] is so confined, meets the stated conditions, and decrypts correctly. Confinement is not a weakness of scale: scaling any baseline law by [MATH] leaves its ordinary Ring-LWE problem exactly equivalent, while the reduced encoder destroys every error it produces. The reduction discrepancy is a multiple of [MATH] and not of [MATH], so the small-error premise of the proof cannot remove it, and at the reported parameters a single error coefficient refutes the identity while satisfying that premise. The centered binomial [MATH] separates the coefficient laws at total variation distance [MATH], and at the reported dimension that distance between the induced polynomial laws is exponentially close to one.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a key recovery attack on the CRT-FHE scheme by exploiting a flaw in the CRT-RLWE transformation that causes error confinement, leading to plaintext recovery without the secret key.
motivation: The authors aim to expose a fundamental insecurity in the CRT-RLWE-based encryption scheme of Pradhan et al., showing that the transformation from Ring-LWE to CRT-RLWE does not preserve hardness.
method: They analyze the CRT function's reduction modulo a coprime modulus and show that errors in a certain range encode to zero, allowing key recovery via a single ring inversion and plaintext recovery from any ciphertext.
result: The attack achieves key recovery and chosen-plaintext advantage, and the error distribution is shown to be not preserved, with a total variation distance exponentially close to one from the intended distribution.
conclusion: The CRT-RLWE scheme is insecure for the assumed error range, and the reduction does not establish equivalence to Ring-LWE, making the scheme unsafe for use.

title: The Trace Field On The Prey Nullcline: Criticality Of Planar Hopf Bifurcations On The Admissible Branch
authors: E. Chan-L\'opez
abstract: ArXiv:2608.22047v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We work with the trace field restricted to the prey nullcline of a planar predator--prey system and reorganize the first Lyapunov coefficient around this local geometry. For a graph first nullcline, we show that [MATH], where [MATH] is the marginal predation rate. Under predator self-damping, this identity localizes Hopf bifurcations to ascending branches of the prey nullcline. Using nullcline-adapted coordinates and Hadamard's lemma, we derive a five-term closed expression for the first Lyapunov coefficient [MATH] that remains valid for predator-dependent functional responses. We establish three distinct structural reduction mechanisms: two are general consequences of the cubic pairing with the critical eigenvectors and nullcline straightening, while the third is specific to the Gause class. Comparing the full coefficient with a [MATH]-affine third-order truncation yields an exact decomposition [MATH], with [MATH] governed by two predator-dependent cubic channels and a positive structural factor. On the Hopf locus, we derive a bridge identity showing that the same quantity [MATH] that localizes the bifurcation also weights the tangential derivative of the trace field in the criticality correction. Exact and high-precision validations for representative predator--prey models reproduce the analytical identities and numerical values.
tldr: This paper analyzes the trace field on the prey nullcline to study the criticality of planar Hopf bifurcations in predator-prey systems.
motivation: The authors aim to reorganize the first Lyapunov coefficient around the local geometry of the nullcline to better understand bifurcation patterns in ecological models.
method: They use nullcline-adapted coordinates and Hadamard's lemma to derive a closed expression for the first Lyapunov coefficient and establish structural reduction mechanisms.
result: The paper derives an exact decomposition of the Lyapunov coefficient and a bridge identity linking bifurcation localization to criticality corrections, validated on representative models.
conclusion: The findings provide new mathematical insights into Hopf bifurcations in predator-prey systems, but are outside the scope of quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Inverted Model Selection In Physics-informed Neural Networks: When A Lower Residual Selects A Worse Solution
authors: Rabiu Musah
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21683v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are commonly evaluated via a single aggregate residual, assuming a smaller residual indicates a better solution. Testing this directly across three constrained PDE systems, I find this assumption can systematically fail. In matched pairs of solvers differing only in whether a defining structural identity is hard-wired or penalized, the penalized variant frequently attains a lower equation residual while violating that identity by several orders of magnitude, causing the exact variant to be falsely ranked worse. Over 64 matched pairs spanning two systems, four network variants, and eight seeds, this inversion occurs in 83\% of cases (95\% Wilson CI: 72--90\%), with rates from 72\% to 94\% across systems. Testing across six architectures--MLP, cPINN, XPINN, hp-VPINN, and physics-informed DeepONet and FNO--inverts the ranking in 46 of 48 pairs, indicating that this variability is problem-dependent rather than specific to the approximator. A third, larger vorticity--streamfunction problem shows the same ordering: the residual-optimal solver violates its structural identity by over six orders above tolerance, despite a residual margin of only 9.37%. Because a scalar loss cannot expose this, I introduce a lexicographic admissibility gate spanning the structural identity, boundary trace, and a solvability integral that must vanish independently of the equation residual. All three must pass before residuals can compete. This gate catches three artifact classes but misses a fourth: a prescribed-structure prior yields fields that pass every single-run check, yet deleting the source term reveals that 97\% of the reported structure survives removal of the physics. Reference data and figures accompany the paper.
tldr: This paper shows that evaluating physics-informed neural networks via a single aggregate residual can systematically fail, as lower residuals often select solutions that violate structural identities.
motivation: The common assumption that a smaller residual indicates a better PINN solution is tested by comparing solvers that either hard-wire or penalize a structural identity.
method: Matched pairs of solvers are compared across multiple network architectures and seeds, and a lexicographic admissibility gate is introduced to enforce structural constraints independently of the equation residual.
result: In 83% of 64 matched pairs, the penalized variant achieved a lower residual but violated the structural identity by orders of magnitude, with the inversion occurring across 46 of 48 architecture pairs.
conclusion: A scalar loss cannot expose structural violations, and while a lexicographic gate helps, it still misses certain artifact classes, emphasizing the need for more robust evaluation methods in PINNs.

title: High-Efficiency Ising Machine With Time-Dimensional Exchange Coupling
authors: Zhengyu Du, Haijie Xu, Kaiming Cai, Zhe Yuan, Yue Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21753v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional probabilistic Ising machines often suffer from inefficient exploration of configuration space, while replica-based quantum Monte Carlo methods reduce sampling bottlenecks at the cost of large hardware overhead. Here we propose a time-dimensional exchange coupling (TEC) that replaces spatial replica coupling with a temporal exchange interaction between successive spin configurations of a single p-bit network. This TEC improves sampling efficiency without duplicating replica hardware. At low temperatures, antiferromagnetic TEC expands sampling range; at high temperatures, ferromagnetic TEC stabilizes the optimal state. For MaxCut problems with up to 2000 vertices, TEC significantly accelerates convergence speed. SPICE simulations confirm hardware feasibility. TEC offers a scalable, hardware-efficient strategy to enhance combinatorial optimization on existing Ising machines.
tldr: This paper proposes a time-dimensional exchange coupling (TEC) technique for probabilistic Ising machines to improve sampling efficiency without hardware duplication.
motivation: Conventional probabilistic Ising machines suffer from inefficient exploration of configuration space, and replica-based quantum Monte Carlo methods reduce sampling bottlenecks at the cost of large hardware overhead.
method: The authors replace spatial replica coupling with a temporal exchange interaction between successive spin configurations of a single p-bit network, using antiferromagnetic TEC at low temperatures and ferromagnetic TEC at high temperatures.
result: For MaxCut problems with up to 2000 vertices, TEC significantly accelerates convergence speed, and SPICE simulations confirm hardware feasibility.
conclusion: TEC offers a scalable, hardware-efficient strategy to enhance combinatorial optimization on existing Ising machines.

title: Feature-domain Fourier Ptychographic Tomography With Dark-field Illumination
authors: Chao Tan, Fangrui Lu, Sechan Park, Hyeonseo Na, Chanseok Lee, Chang-Seok Kim, Jeesu Kim, Hwidon Lee, Mooseok Jang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fourier ptychographic tomography (FPT) is an implementation of intensity diffraction tomography that reconstructs three-dimensional (3D) refractive-index (RI) distributions from angle-varied intensity measurements. The distinctive advantage of FPT emerges when incorporating dark-field illumination, which extends the space-bandwidth product toward gigavoxel-scale volumetric imaging, yet dark-field measurements are highly sensitive to system imperfections and often have low signal-to-noise ratios. Here, we propose feature-domain FPT (FD-FPT), which evaluates data fidelity after feature extraction and is optimized using automatic differentiation. In numerical and experimental tests, FD-FPT resolves structures near the synthetic-aperture cutoff far more reliably than the spatial-domain baseline (SD-FPT). Notably, in a whole-mount Oedogonium specimen, the reticulate chloroplast network and transverse septa were resolved only by FD-FPT. We further demonstrate a 1.81-gigavoxel RI reconstruction of a mouse adrenal gland section across a 1.66 by 1.40 square millimeter field of view, establishing FD-FPT as a practical route to label-free volumetric imaging that combines millimeter-scale coverage with cellular-scale structural contrast.
tldr: This paper proposes feature-domain Fourier ptychographic tomography (FD-FPT) for improved 3D refractive index reconstruction with dark-field illumination, demonstrating higher reliability and gigavoxel-scale imaging.
motivation: Fourier ptychographic tomography (FPT) reconstructs 3D refractive index distributions from angle-varied intensity measurements, and dark-field illumination extends its space-bandwidth product but suffers from sensitivity to system imperfections and low signal-to-noise ratios.
method: The authors introduce FD-FPT, which evaluates data fidelity after feature extraction and optimizes the reconstruction using automatic differentiation, in contrast to the spatial-domain baseline.
result: Numerical and experimental tests show that FD-FPT resolves structures near the synthetic-aperture cutoff more reliably than the spatial-domain baseline, and it successfully reconstructed a 1.81-gigavoxel mouse adrenal gland section.
conclusion: FD-FPT provides a practical route to label-free volumetric imaging with millimeter-scale coverage and cellular-scale structural contrast.

title: New Laplace Convolution Integrals Involving Exponential, Error, And Parabolic Cylinder Functions With Applications In Heat Transfer And Linear Viscoelasticity
authors: Juan Luis Gonz\'{a}lez Santander
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute several new Laplace convolution integrals involving exponential functions, error functions, and parabolic cylinder functions. We extend our results using formulas for repeated integration and differentiation. We apply these convolution integrals to heat transfer and linear viscoelastic problems. As a by-product, we obtain new integral representations for the error function and the complementary error function.
tldr: The paper presents new Laplace convolution integrals involving exponential, error, and parabolic cylinder functions, with applications to heat transfer and linear viscoelasticity.
motivation: The author aims to extend the toolkit of Laplace convolution integrals for applied mathematics, providing exact solutions that can be used in physical problems such as heat conduction and viscoelastic response.
method: The methodology relies on Laplace transform techniques, properties of special functions (error, complementary error, parabolic cylinder), and rules for repeated integration and differentiation of transforms.
result: New convolution integrals are computed, and as a by-product, novel integral representations for the error function and complementary error function are obtained.
conclusion: The derived formulas are applied to heat transfer and linear viscoelasticity problems, demonstrating their practical utility and expanding the mathematical resources available for such analyses.

title: On Characterizations, Decompositions, And Stability Of Convex Sequences
authors: Angshuman R. Goswami
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces new characterizations, decomposition theorems, and stability results for convex sequences. We show that a sequence is convex precisely when its epigraph satisfies a midpoint convexity condition, thereby connecting discrete and geometric notions of convexity. A decomposition result proves that any sequence can be written as the difference of two convex sequences, with generalizations to higher-order convexity. We construct nontrivial convex minorants for bounded-below sequences and establish a Hyers-Ulam-type stability theorem showing that any approximately convex sequence can be uniformly approximated by a genuine convex sequence without significantly altering its values. Finally, for a concave sequence, we characterize those subsequences that are convex in it by providing slope inequalities and monotone auxiliary sequences. We explore the interplay among convexity, subadditivity, and periodically indexed subsequences.
tldr: This paper introduces new characterizations, decompositions, and stability results for convex sequences, connecting discrete and geometric convexity.
motivation: The author aims to explore the theoretical properties of convex sequences and provide tools for approximating approximately convex sequences.
method: The paper uses midpoint convexity, decomposition into differences of convex sequences, construction of convex minorants, and Hyers-Ulam stability theorems.
result: Establishes that convexity is equivalent to a midpoint convexity condition on the epigraph, proves a decomposition theorem for any sequence into differences of convex sequences, constructs convex minorants for bounded-below sequences, and provides a Hyers-Ulam-type stability result for approximately convex sequences.
conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive mathematical framework for convex sequences, with implications for analysis and approximation theory.

title: Bent Functions And The Completed Maiorana-McFarland Class
authors: Enes Pasalic, Alexandr Polujan, Fengrong Zhang, Sadmir Kudin
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21461v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we survey some fundamental results and recent advances in the design and analysis of Boolean bent functions from the perspective of their relation to the completed Maiorana-McFarland class.
tldr: A survey of Boolean bent functions and their connection to the completed Maiorana-McFarland class.
motivation: To review fundamental results and recent advances in bent functions, focusing on their relation to the Maiorana-McFarland class.
method: Survey and analysis of existing literature on bent functions and the completed Maiorana-McFarland class.
result: Summarizes key results and advances in the design and analysis of bent functions within this class.
conclusion: Provides a comprehensive overview of bent functions related to the Maiorana-McFarland class.

title: A Memory-Efficient Adjoint State Optimization Method Based On Time-Reversible Dynamical Low-Rank Approximation
authors: Julian Mangott Lukas Einkemmer
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The primary challenge of conducting PDE-constrained optimization for high-dimensional problems, such as kinetic equations, is the often prohibitive memory cost. Computing gradients using the adjoint state method would require the storage of the entire time history of the forward solution. For such problems, where the memory cost for storing a single instance of the forward solution can already be a limiting factor, this is clearly not feasible. In this paper, we propose a memory-efficient adjoint state method that compresses the forward and adjoint solution with a dynamical low-rank approximation (a model order reduction technique) and bypasses the need to store the entire forward solution by employing a time-reversible low-rank integrator. The dynamical low-rank approach introduces a number of challenges: reversibility can fail in the rank-deficient case and the low-rank trajectories can show chaotic behavior. In particular, the latter has a number of important consequences for the optimization problem. We address those challenges and show that our method can drastically reduce the memory requirement for gradient-based optimization of kinetic equations. In particular, we consider two examples from kinetic plasma physics: optimizing beam profiles to suppress a bump-on-tail instability and shaping a particle beam using external electric fields.
tldr: The paper introduces a memory-efficient adjoint state method using time-reversible dynamical low-rank approximation to reduce memory cost in PDE-constrained optimization for kinetic equations.
motivation: The prohibitive memory cost of storing the full time history of forward solutions in high-dimensional kinetic optimization problems motivates this work.
method: The method compresses forward and adjoint solutions via dynamical low-rank approximation and employs a time-reversible low-rank integrator, addressing challenges like rank deficiency and chaotic behavior.
result: The approach drastically reduces memory requirements for gradient-based optimization and is demonstrated on kinetic plasma physics examples.
conclusion: The method enables feasible optimization for high-dimensional kinetic equations by overcoming memory bottlenecks, despite complications from low-rank dynamics.

title: Average Finite-Blocklength Packet Error Rate Over Nakagami-$m$ Fading Via A Logistic--Lerch Approximation
authors: Aamir Mahmood
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21564v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluating the average packet error rate (PER) of finite-blocklength (FBL) coded transmission over fading requires integrating the block-error waterfall, given by the normal approximation, against the fading distribution, which is intractable for general Nakagami-[MATH] channels. This letter approximates the conditional waterfall by a slope-matched logistic function and shows that its Nakagami-[MATH] average reduces to a single Lerch-transcendent term that interpolates between the FBL waterfall and the classical outage limit, with norming constants explicit in rate and blocklength. The closed form supports non-integer fading and, composed into an effective-capacity objective, yields a quality-of-service (QoS) aware rate-selection rule. It matches the normal-approximation integral to about 1\% uniformly in [MATH] over the nominal FBL operating region, while outage and linearization baselines exceed several percent at high diversity.
tldr: Presents a closed-form approximation for the average finite-blocklength packet error rate over Nakagami-m fading using a logistic function and Lerch transcendent.
motivation: Computing the average packet error rate (PER) for finite-blocklength (FBL) coded transmission over fading requires an intractable integral against the fading distribution.
method: Approximates the conditional block-error waterfall by a slope-matched logistic function, then averages it over Nakagami-m fading to obtain a single Lerch-transcendent term.
result: The closed form matches the normal-approximation integral within about 1% across the FBL operating region and outperforms outage and linearization baselines at high diversity.
conclusion: The approximation enables QoS-aware rate selection and extends to non-integer fading parameters, offering a practical tool for FBL performance evaluation in fading channels.

title: A Data-Driven Computational Framework For Incompressible Flow In Hydraulic Networks
authors: Pedro B. Bazon, Cristian G. Gebhardt, Roberto F. Ausas
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21575v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical procedure for solving hydraulic networks relies on the assumption of constitutive equations, which state the relationship between the pressure gradient and fluxes along an edge. In this paper, we propose a data-driven framework that bypasses these constitutive models, formulating the incompressible flow problem directly on the graph topology. By assigning discrete measured data points to network edges, the problem is cast as a mixed-integer quadratic optimization over nodal pressures, edgewise states, and data assignments, accommodating both laminar (convex) and turbulent (non-convex) regimes. To solve this, we evaluate three algorithms: a GPU-accelerated Brute Force method, the Alternating Direction Method (ADM), and Deterministic Annealing (DA). The Brute Force method certifies global optima for small networks, establishing a good baseline for the iterative solvers. We demonstrate that ADM is highly sensitive to its initialization, requiring a faithful surrogate model to avoid local minima. In contrast, DA eliminates this dependence through unsupervised clustering. By annealing the data assignment from the centroid to strict nearest-neighbor projections, DA consistently reaches the global optimum without prior manifold reconstruction. Furthermore, numerical experiments reveal that DA is robust to noisy data, remains thermodynamically admissible on all but the coarsest and noisiest datasets, and sustains its convergence rate on larger networks where Brute Force is intractable and ADM degrades. Finally, the framework is successfully validated on complex configurations, including mixed-component networks and a [MATH]-edge arteriovenous bed featuring a non-Newtonian Carreau--Yasuda model, demonstrating its scalability and practical applicability.
tldr: The paper introduces a data-driven computational framework for solving incompressible flow in hydraulic networks, bypassing traditional constitutive equations and using mixed-integer quadratic optimization.
motivation: Classical hydraulic network solvers rely on constitutive equations connecting pressure and flux; this work aims to replace them with data-driven approaches.
method: The problem is formulated as a mixed-integer quadratic optimization over nodal pressures and edge states, and three algorithms (Brute Force, ADM, Deterministic Annealing) are evaluated for solving it.
result: Deterministic Annealing consistently finds global optima without initialization dependence, is robust to noise, and scales to larger networks where other methods degrade.
conclusion: The framework is validated on complex networks including non-Newtonian flows, demonstrating practical applicability and scalability.

title: An Elegant Analytical Resolution Of The Sprott-Zeraoulia Conjecture For Three-Dimensional Quadratic Differential Systems With Symmetric Jacobian Matrices
authors: Rafael Paulino Silva Marcelo Messias
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21681v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Sprott--Zeraoulia conjecture, formulated on the basis of numerical experiments, states that three-dimensional quadratic continuous-time systems with symmetric Jacobian matrices cannot exhibit chaotic behavior. We give an analytical resolution of this conjecture in terms of the principal precise notions of chaos used for continuous dynamical systems. The starting point is the classical, but decisive, fact that symmetry of the Jacobian on [MATH] is equivalent to a global gradient representation. Hence every system in the conjectured class can be written as [MATH], where [MATH] is a polynomial of degree at most three, and the conjecture becomes a problem about cubic polynomial gradient flows. For bounded trajectories, the monotonicity property of gradient systems first confines every omega-limit set to a critical level of [MATH]. When the equilibria on that level are isolated, convergence follows from the connectedness of the omega-limit set. In the general case, which may include curves or surfaces of equilibria, the \L{}ojasiewicz gradient inequality implies finite length and convergence of every bounded forward trajectory to a single equilibrium. Consequently, compact invariant sets support no nonstationary recurrence, positive-entropy measure, topological transitivity, Smale horseshoe, or Devaney, Auslander--Yorke, Li--Yorke, mean Li--Yorke, and distributional chaos. Solutions escaping to infinity are treated through the Poincar\'e compactification. Finally, we connect the gradient formulation with earlier Darboux-theoretic criteria: invariant algebraic surfaces satisfy [MATH], and an invariant affine plane with constant cofactor produces an exact tangential--normal decomposition of the potential and the flow.
tldr: This paper analytically proves that three-dimensional quadratic systems with symmetric Jacobian matrices cannot exhibit chaotic behavior, confirming the Sprott-Zeraoulia conjecture.
motivation: The conjecture was based on numerical experiments, and a rigorous analytical proof was needed to settle the question of chaos in such systems.
method: By showing that symmetric Jacobian implies a gradient representation, the authors use monotonicity and the Lojasiewicz gradient inequality to prove that every bounded forward trajectory converges to a single equilibrium.
result: Bounded trajectories converge to equilibria, ruling out all forms of non-stationary recurrence, positive-entropy, topological transitivity, and various chaos notions (Devaney, Li-Yorke, etc.).
conclusion: The conjecture is true; the proof also connects gradient formulation with Darboux integrability criteria.

title: A Counterexample To Global Convergence Of Classical Dfp Under The Standard Strong Wolfe Conditions
authors: Benqi Liu, Zichen Wang, Zaiwen Wen, Liwei Zhang, Yaxiang Yuan
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21708v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A long-standing open question in quasi-Newton optimization asks whether the classical Davidon--Fletcher--Powell (DFP) method converges globally on uniformly convex objectives when all accepted steps satisfy the standard weak Wolfe conditions. We show that the answer is no, even under the standard strong Wolfe conditions. Fix [MATH] and [MATH]. We construct a function [MATH] such that [MATH] for all [MATH]. We also choose a fixed positive definite initial inverse Hessian approximation and a sequence of positive step lengths. The classical DFP iteration is well defined, and all accepted steps satisfy the standard strong Wolfe conditions, but [MATH] converges to a positive constant. The global Hessian condition number is at most three. The construction uses an alternating two-step DFP sequence near a one-dimensional invariant center manifold. Along this sequence, the smaller eigenvalue of the inverse Hessian approximation tends to zero. The changes in the gradient norm between cycle starts are summable, but the total rotation of the associated eigenvectors is unbounded. The accumulation points of the DFP sequence form a circle. A uniform separation bound allows us to interpolate the prescribed function values and gradients. We add smooth functions with pairwise disjoint supports to a quadratic and keep the global Hessian bounds. An affine change of variables gives an identity-initialized example with problem-dependent Hessian bounds. An orthogonal direct sum extends the result to every dimension [MATH].
tldr: This paper constructs a counterexample showing that the classical DFP quasi-Newton method fails to converge globally even under standard strong Wolfe conditions, answering a long-standing open question negatively.
motivation: The paper addresses a long-standing open question in optimization about whether the DFP method converges globally on uniformly convex objectives when all accepted steps satisfy Wolfe conditions.
method: The authors construct a specific smooth function and a fixed positive definite initial inverse Hessian approximation, along with a sequence of step lengths, such that the DFP iteration is well-defined and satisfies strong Wolfe conditions but converges to a circle rather than a minimum.
result: The DFP iterates do not converge to the optimizer; the global Hessian condition number is at most three, and the accumulation points form a circle, with unbounded rotation of eigenvectors.
conclusion: This provides a counterexample to global convergence of DFP under standard Wolfe conditions, extendable to any dimension via an orthogonal direct sum.

title: Optimal Selling Of Defaultable Assets Using The Distribution Builder
authors: Stephan Sturm Sixian Jin
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the problem of when it is best to sell a risky asset in the framework of the approach under the consideration of potential ruin. This approach allows investors to express their preferences directly as a desired target distribution without first specifying a risk aversion or utility function. Mathematically, the problem is closely related to the Skorokhod embedding problem, where the goal is to attain a given distribution by stopping a diffusion process. We work in a general framework of one-dimensional diffusion processes and extend existing results to include the possibility of ruin. We first provide a full characterization of the set of distributions that can be attained before ruin occurs. Then, we formulate two optimization problems that tackle the issue of what to do if the originally specified distribution is either not attainable or not optimal: finding the attainable distribution closest to an unattainable distribution and selecting an optimal attainable distribution under first-order stochastic dominance constraints if the originally specified distribution is attainable, but not optimal. We show existence and uniqueness of solutions to these constrained convex optimization problems in an extended [MATH]-divergence framework, provide an analytic characterization of solutions and give numerical examples.
tldr: This paper extends the distribution builder approach to optimal selling of defaultable assets, considering potential ruin and using Skorokhod embedding.
motivation: The authors aim to provide a method for investors to express their preferences as a target distribution without specifying a utility function, while accounting for the possibility of ruin.
method: The work models the asset price as a one-dimensional diffusion process and characterizes attainable distributions before ruin, then formulates and solves convex optimization problems for unattainable or suboptimal target distributions.
result: Existence, uniqueness, and analytic characterization of solutions are established in an extended f-divergence framework, with numerical examples provided.
conclusion: The framework successfully incorporates ruin into the distribution builder approach, offering a novel tool for optimal selling decisions in defaultable asset markets.

title: Wasserstein Moment Nudging For Vlasov-Poisson Data Assimilation
authors: Liyao Lyu, Xinyue Yu, David Schneidinger, Hayden Schaeffer
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a continuous data assimilation method for particle-in-cell simulations of the Vlasov-Poisson equation when only hydrodynamic moments are observed. The forecast state is an empirical measure on phase space, whereas the observed fields (density, bulk velocity, and temperature) constrain only a few velocity moments and leave the velocity-space shape of the distribution undetermined. We construct the moment feedback as a Wasserstein gradient flow of a moment-mismatch functional over phase-space measures. The resulting drift acts directly on particle positions and velocities, couples the density, momentum, and energy residuals through a single variational structure, and vanishes on the entire moment-compatible set. Under the standard Wasserstein metric, the energy residual produces a position correction that grows quadratically with the particle speed, and the particle system falls outside standard well-posedness theory. Our primary formulation pairs the quadratic moment mismatch with a velocity-weighted Wasserstein metric that penalizes spatial transport at large peculiar velocity relative to the observed bulk flow, which removes this growth. A direction-split variant retains the plain metric instead. Under the same weighted metric, an alternative moment-relative-entropy functional yields an affine, shape-preserving velocity correction and explicit global moment balances for the space-inhomogeneous system. We prove that the finite-particle scheme with linear Lenard-Bernstein collisions is globally well posed.
