tldr: This paper designs randomized strategyproof mechanisms for multi-facility location, achieving improved approximation ratios for two facilities and beyond.
motivation: To design strategyproof mechanisms for multi-facility location with low social cost, improving upon existing benchmarks.
method: Introduces several mechanisms: Pairwise-Distance and Hybrid-Distance for two facilities on Ptolemaic spaces, Inverse-Square for k=n-1 facilities, and Gap-Product for k facilities on the line.
result: Achieves approximation ratios of 4 and 3.5186 for two facilities, breaking the previous factor-4 benchmark, and constant approximation for k=3 on the line, improving previous n-dependent guarantees.
conclusion: The proposed mechanisms are strategyproof and outperform existing ones, providing tighter bounds.

title: Syntax Element Encryption For H.265/hevc Using Chaotic Map-Based Coefficient Scrambling Scheme
authors: Liang-Wei Li, Chung-Nan Lee, Kishu Gupta, Huei-Fang Yang, Ashutosh Kumar Singh
abstract: ArXiv:2608.22573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In today's digital landscape, high-efficiency video coding (H.265/HEVC) has emerged as the most widely used video coding standard, employing selective encryption schemes to protect the privacy of video content while maintaining efficient compression performance. However, existing coefficient scrambling methods impose a significant computational load, leading to increased bit rate overhead due to encryption, longer execution times, and insufficient safety measures. To address these issues, a new coefficient scrambling scheme based on is proposed. This approach leverages the pseudorandomness, ergodicity, and sensitivity to initial conditions inherent in chaotic maps to generate highly unpredictable coefficient distributions, thereby strengthening security while preserving low complexity. Unlike conventional scrambling, chaotic maps ensure minimal correlation between encrypted coefficients, enhancing resistance against statistical and differential attacks. Additionally, the scrambling conditions are specifically designed to minimize the impact on the bit rate overhead. Furthermore, when combined with syntax element encryption (SEC), which includes motion vector difference (MVD), quantized transform coefficients (QTC), and luma intraprediction mode (Luma IPM), this method effectively distorts video content. The proposed scheme operates synchronously with slices, ensuring that the decryption of video content remains intact even if some slices are lost. Additionally, a random sequence generated by AES-CTR is incorporated with the H.265 encoded stream to protect against chosen-plaintext attacks.
tldr: This paper proposes a chaotic map-based coefficient scrambling scheme for H.265/HEVC video encryption to reduce bit rate overhead and enhance security.
motivation: Existing coefficient scrambling methods in H.265/HEVC impose computational load and increase bit rate overhead, and lack sufficient security.
method: The method uses chaotic maps to generate unpredictable coefficient distributions, combines with syntax element encryption (MVD, QTC, Luma IPM), and incorporates AES-CTR to protect against chosen-plaintext attacks.
result: The scheme strengthens security against statistical and differential attacks, minimizes bit rate overhead, and maintains low complexity.
conclusion: The proposed scheme effectively distorts video content and operates synchronously with slices to ensure decryption integrity even with slice loss.

title: Reasoning With Probabilities: Relating Weighted Model Counting And Probabilistic Model Checking
authors: Vincent Derkinderen Bahare Salmani
abstract: ArXiv:2608.22632v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Weighted model counting (WMC) and probabilistic model checking (PMC) are two well- established frameworks that are independently developed, the former for probabilistic inference, the latter traditionally for probabilistic verification, though recently also applied to inference. The formal relationship between the two frameworks, however, remains largely unexplored. In this paper, we lay the foundations for how they relate: we present (1) a mapping from cycle- free parametric Markov chains (pMCs) to arithmetic circuits (ACs), enabling the reduction of reachability probability computations in such pMCs to a weighted model counting problem on the corresponding ACs, and (2) a mapping from a subclass of arithmetic circuits -- with probabilistic semantics -- back to parametric Markov chains. We propose a detailed correspondence between the entities of WMC and PMC, and discuss how our mappings enable transferring optimization techniques such as bisimulation minimization across the frameworks.
tldr: This paper establishes formal mappings between weighted model counting and probabilistic model checking, linking parametric Markov chains to arithmetic circuits.
motivation: To explore the relationship between two independently developed probabilistic reasoning frameworks and enable transfer of optimization techniques.
method: Introduces a mapping from cycle-free parametric Markov chains to arithmetic circuits, reducing reachability probability computations to weighted model counting, and a reverse mapping from a subclass of arithmetic circuits back to parametric Markov chains.
result: Provides a detailed correspondence between entities of WMC and PMC, facilitating transfer of techniques like bisimulation minimization across frameworks.
conclusion: The foundations established could enable cross-fertilization between weighted model counting and probabilistic model checking, potentially advancing probabilistic inference and verification.

title: Obscura-PQ: Post-Quantum Privacy-Preserving Protocol For The Algorand Blockchain Using Lattice-Based Linkable Ring Signatures
authors: Navid Azimi
abstract: ArXiv:2608.22645v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Public blockchains expose the complete transaction graph, and the privacy protocols deployed to obscure it rely almost exclusively on elliptic-curve cryptography, whose discrete-logarithm foundations fall to Shor's algorithm. Because ledgers are immutable, every anonymity set published today under classical assumptions can be retroactively deanonymized by a future quantum adversary. Transitioning to post-quantum alternatives remains challenging, as strict smart-contract resource limits prohibit native on-chain verification of computationally intensive post-quantum proofs. To address these challenges, we present , a decentralized, non-custodial post-quantum privacy protocol that verifies natively on the Algorand blockchain. Its core is a setup-free lattice linkable ring signature over the cyclotomic ring [MATH]. A deposit is a Ring-SIS binding commitment to a short secret; a withdrawal proves knowledge of a ring opening via an AOS/Borromean-style challenge chain over two response-sharing linear relations with rejection-sampled short responses, while publishing a deterministic Ring-LWE serial number for double-spend detection. We reduce double-spend soundness and linkability to Ring-SIS, theft resistance to Ring-SIS for honestly generated deposits, and anonymity to Ring-LWE and an explicit decisional linking assumption in the classical random-oracle model. To overcome strict on-chain opcode and storage limits, Obscura-PQ evaluates verification relations entirely in the NTT domain. We split forward NTTs across opcode-pooled execution phases and stream oversized proofs through refundable box storage, enabling [MATH] membership and double-spend checks. We provide a complete Algorand testnet implementation, demonstrating native on-chain verification of a post-quantum privacy protocol under strict smart-contract limits.
tldr: This paper presents a post-quantum privacy protocol for the Algorand blockchain using lattice-based linkable ring signatures and native on-chain verification.
motivation: Because classical elliptic curve cryptography is vulnerable to quantum attacks, and blockchain ledgers are immutable, existing privacy protocols can be deanonymized by future quantum adversaries. The paper aims to provide a post-quantum privacy-preserving protocol that can be verified on-chain under strict smart-contract resource limits.
method: The protocol uses a setup-free lattice linkable ring signature over a cyclotomic ring, with Ring-SIS binding commitments, rejection-sampled short responses, and Ring-LWE serial numbers for double-spend detection. On-chain verification is performed entirely in the NTT domain to overcome resource limits, using opcode-pooled execution phases and refundable box storage for streaming proofs.
result: The authors provide a complete Algorand testnet implementation demonstrating native on-chain verification of a post-quantum privacy protocol under strict smart-contract limits.
conclusion: The work addresses the challenge of implementing post-quantum privacy on blockchains, but it is not related to the specified research directions.

title: Step Recursion: Resource Profiles And Descent Quotients
authors: Kirill Osipov
abstract: ArXiv:2608.22662v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a resource representation for step recursion in which mutable-state width and recursion descent are explicit and independent parameters. A width bound [MATH] controls the size of the encoded machine state, while an effective descent [MATH] determines the available recursion depth [MATH]. For generalized-inverse descents, we derive the depth directly from generator growth and characterize the increasing sequences that can occur as generator orbits. We then connect this depth--width geometry to standard finite-branching computation. Every deterministic bounded-state dynamics is realizable by a single ordinary bounded step recursion over a fixed finite numerical basis. Using deterministic, existential, universal, or alternating aggregation on the same local dynamics yields the corresponding machine semantics. After closure under the width reparameterizations needed to absorb fixed local cost, the resulting language classes are exactly the machine time--space classes on profiles [MATH]. Finally, profile domination quotients effective descents by admissible width reparameterization. Some depth curves collapse, yet polynomial widths support an explicit infinite strict hierarchy between the canonical polynomial- and exponential-depth profiles. Thus descent remains a nonredundant resource coordinate after polynomial width reparameterization; standard complexity classes are calibration points.
tldr: Develops a resource representation for step recursion with explicit width and descent parameters, relating recursion depth to finite-branching computation and characterizing complexity classes.
motivation: To understand how recursion depth and state width interact as resource coordinates, and to relate recursion-based computation to standard machine complexity classes.
method: Introduces a notion of step recursion with mutable-state width and descent; derives descent depth from generator growth; uses width reparameterization to absorb local costs; analyzes profiles and quotient relations.
result: Shows that deterministic bounded-state dynamics are realizable by bounded step recursion, and that after closure, the language classes correspond to machine time-space classes. Establishes a strict hierarchy of polynomial-width profiles.
conclusion: Descent is a nonredundant resource coordinate even after polynomial width reparameterization, providing new insights into recursion-based computation.

title: Kontograph: Verified Point-in-Time Feature Consistency And Amortised Explanation For Real-Time Anti-Money Laundering Under A 200 Ms Decision Budget
authors: Ahmed Abolfadl
abstract: ArXiv:2608.22389v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Regulation (EU) 2024/886 obliges European payment service providers to settle euro credit transfers in under ten seconds, around the clock. This removes both the overnight batch window in which anti-money-laundering (AML) analytics traditionally ran and the settlement delay that made recovery possible, forcing detection, explanation and decision inside a single-digit-second envelope. We present KONTOGRAPH, an end-to-end AML pipeline for the SEPA Instant rail built under a self-imposed 200 ms 99th-percentile budget, and report an empirical study on 1,562,860 simulated payments with injected typologies and deliberately incomplete labels. Three findings are of interest beyond the system itself. First, a temporal graph network with per-node memory improves PR-AUC over a gradient-boosted tabular baseline from 0.0053 to 0.1717, a paired day-blocked bootstrap difference of +0.166 with 95% CI [0.105, 0.241]; per-node memory alone more than doubles the score. Second, expressing each feature once and compiling it to three execution backends, with equivalence enforced by property-based tests that perturb the future, surfaced three point-in-time violations that code review had passed--each of which would have inflated reported performance. Third, and most consequential for practice, exporting the deployed tree ensemble to ONNX changed only [MATH] in mean score yet altered 0.26% of decisions and inflated the alert volume by 12%, because 32-bit accumulation perturbs scores across a cost-optimal threshold of [MATH]. We argue that a serving-format conversion must be treated as a model change until measured, and that fidelity metrics for subgraph explainers can be vacuous when candidate neighbourhoods are small--a null result we report in full.
tldr: A real-time anti-money laundering pipeline using temporal graph networks under a 200ms budget that addresses point-in-time feature consistency and the impact of model serving format conversions.
motivation: EU regulation mandates instant payments, removing batch windows for AML analytics, so detection, explanation, and decision must occur within seconds.
method: Built KONTOGRAPH, an end-to-end pipeline with a temporal graph network and per-node memory, using property-based tests for feature consistency and analyzing the effect of ONNX model export.
result: The temporal graph network improved PR-AUC from 0.0053 to 0.1717 over a tabular baseline; identified three point-in-time violations; ONNX conversion changed 0.26% of decisions and inflated alert volume by 12%.
conclusion: Serving-format conversion must be treated as a model change until measured, and explanation fidelity metrics can be misleading for small candidate neighbourhoods.

title: Inner Product Bounds Via The Moore-Penrose Inverse With Applications
authors: A. Sheikhhosseini, Gh. Aghamollaei, M. Sababheh
abstract: ArXiv:2608.22220v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, by implementing the generalized inverse, known as the Moore-Penrose inverse, for Hilbert space operators, several inner product bounds that are of Cauchy-Schwarz type are presented. As a standard application, some new refined and generalized versions of numerical radius-norm bounds are also stated, in a generalized form that involves different combinations of operators.
tldr: This paper presents inner product bounds of Cauchy-Schwarz type using the Moore-Penrose inverse for Hilbert space operators, with applications to numerical radius-norm bounds.
motivation: The motivation is to derive new operator inequalities that generalize and refine classical results, potentially useful in operator theory and related fields.
method: The method uses the Moore-Penrose generalized inverse to establish several inner product inequalities, from which refined numerical radius bounds are derived.
result: The paper obtains new refined and generalized versions of numerical radius-norm bounds involving combinations of operators.
conclusion: The results contribute to the theory of operator inequalities but are not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: On The Parabolic Fatou Domains Ii: Rigidity
authors: Ning Gao, Yan Gao, Wenjuan Peng
abstract: ArXiv:2608.22328v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is a follow-up study on the holomorphic model problem for infinitely-connected parabolic Fatou domains of rational maps. We prove that simple parabolic maps serve as holomorphic models for such parabolic Fatou domains. Moreover, we show that every simple parabolic map can be perturbed into a rational map with a completely invariant attracting Fatou domain without changing the topology of the Julia set, thereby confirming the Goldberg--Milnor conjecture for simple parabolic maps.
tldr: This paper studies parabolic Fatou domains of rational maps and proves rigidity results for simple parabolic maps, confirming the Goldberg-Milnor conjecture in that case.
motivation: To understand the holomorphic model problem for infinitely-connected parabolic Fatou domains and the rigidity of simple parabolic maps.
method: The paper uses complex dynamics methods, including analysis of parabolic maps and their Julia sets, and topological arguments about perturbations.
result: Simple parabolic maps serve as holomorphic models for such domains, and they can be perturbed to rational maps with completely invariant attracting Fatou domains without changing the topology of the Julia set, confirming the Goldberg-Milnor conjecture for simple parabolic maps.
conclusion: The Goldberg-Milnor conjecture holds for simple parabolic maps, and the paper provides insight into the structure of parabolic Fatou domains.

title: On Convergence Of An Accelerated Modified Newton Method For Nonlinear Equations
authors: Sanwar Ahmad, Joy Watson, Mohammad Tabanjeh
abstract: ArXiv:2608.22060v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Newton's iteration is a fundamental tool for root-finding and numerical solutions of systems of equations. The iteration rapidly refines the initial approximation to the exact root, and in general the convergence is quadratic. Since the method requires finding the function value and its derivative at each iteration, in some cases, it may not converge. This is because the value of the derivative gets close to zero. In this paper, we introduce a modified and stable algorithm of Newton's iteration method that addresses this issue, reduces computational cost, and improves efficiency. In addition. we analyze the convergence properties of the modified method to demonstrate its effectiveness.
tldr: Introduces a modified Newton's method for solving nonlinear equations that addresses divergence issues when the derivative is near zero.
motivation: Standard Newton's method can fail to converge when the derivative approaches zero; a stable and efficient alternative is needed.
method: Proposes a modified and stable algorithm, analyzing its convergence properties to demonstrate effectiveness.
result: The modified method improves stability and reduces computational cost compared to the classical Newton's method.
conclusion: The modified Newton's method is a viable alternative for nonlinear equations, particularly in challenging derivative scenarios.

title: Antagonistic Control: Foundations, Scalability And Nonlinearity
authors: Andr\'e M. H. Teixeira Sribalaji C. Anand
abstract: ArXiv:2608.22204v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the worst-case impact of constrained control inputs: an input seeks to maximize the average cost of some outputs, measured in the [MATH] or [MATH] norm, while remaining bounded in terms of other outputs. This problem template subsumes classical metrics such as the [MATH] norm and the output-to-output gain, and arises in adversarial control, security assessment, and robust control. For linear time-invariant systems, we provide an exact semi-definite program (SDP) when there is a single constraint, and SDPs computing upper bounds when there are multiple constraints. We derive sufficient conditions, in terms of system zeros and relative degrees, under which the worst-case cost is unbounded, together with a constructive closed-loop modification that removes the unboundedness. From a security standpoint, unbounded values reveal structural limitations in detecting certain attack inputs. For positive systems, we provide scalable formulations whose complexity grows linearly in the state dimension: a scalable SDP for quadratic costs, and an exact linear program for linear costs. The results extend to nonlinear polynomial systems via a sum-of-squares program. We illustrate the results with numerical examples.
tldr: This paper studies the worst-case impact of constrained control inputs on system outputs, providing exact and scalable SDP formulations for linear, positive, and polynomial nonlinear systems.
motivation: To understand and mitigate adversarial inputs in control systems, with applications to security assessment and robust control.
method: Uses semidefinite programming (SDP) for linear systems, scalable formulations for positive systems, and sum-of-squares for polynomial nonlinear systems.
result: Provides exact SDP for single constraints, upper bounds for multiple constraints, conditions for unbounded worst-case cost, and scalable formulations with linear complexity in state dimension.
conclusion: The results reveal structural limitations in detecting certain attack inputs and offer computationally efficient tools for worst-case analysis in control.

title: Explainable Adaptive Zero Trust Framework For Aws With Adversarial Robustness Evaluation
authors: Om Singh, Yagyaraj Pandey, Nandini Pathak
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21477v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cloud environments built on Amazon Web Services face a structural security vulnerability: once a credential passes authentication, the resulting session is often treated as trusted for its entire duration. This assumption fails when credentials are stolen. We introduce the Explainable Adaptive Zero Trust Framework (EAZTF), a cloud-native security layer that continuously reevaluates the legitimacy of API actions throughout a session. EAZTF combines Isolation Forest and XGBoost to evaluate eight CloudTrail and IAM-derived behavioral features in real time and produce a Trust Risk Score (TRS) that determines whether a session continues, requires step-up MFA, or is restricted. Each decision is accompanied by a SHAP or LIME explanation, providing human-readable audit records for security analysis and compliance. The framework is also evaluated against four adversarial evasion strategies: credential theft, behavioral mimicry, API rate evasion, and privilege escalation. Experiments on an 8,500-record synthetic CloudTrail dataset show that Isolation Forest achieves 94.4% precision, 91.2% recall, and an F1 score of 0.928. Across the four adversarial scenarios, the mean detection rate is 91.0%, with behavioral mimicry being the most difficult at 83.9%. SHAP analysis identifies IP reputation, login-time deviation, and API call velocity as the three dominant features. A structured NIST SP 800-207 self-assessment gives EAZTF a mean compliance score of 93%, compared with 38% for a traditional perimeter baseline. Mean time to detect decreases from hours to under one minute. Because the evaluation uses synthetic data, these results should be interpreted as indicative rather than validated production performance.
tldr: A machine-learning-based zero trust framework for AWS that evaluates API actions in real-time with SHAP explanations and adversarial robustness analysis.
motivation: Cloud environments like AWS have a security flaw where authenticated sessions are trusted for the entire duration, vulnerable to credential theft; the paper aims to continuously re-evaluate session legitimacy.
method: Combines Isolation Forest and XGBoost on eight behavioral features from CloudTrail/IAM to produce a Trust Risk Score (TRS), with SHAP/LIME explanations; evaluates against four adversarial evasion strategies on synthetic data.
result: Isolation Forest achieves 94.4% precision, 91.2% recall, F1 0.928; mean detection rate across adversarial scenarios is 91.0%; NIST SP 800-207 compliance score 93% vs 38% baseline; MTD reduces to under a minute.
conclusion: The framework shows promising results for adaptive zero trust in AWS, but since evaluation is on synthetic data, results are indicative, not production-validated.

title: Beyond Over-Refusal: Defending Indirect Prompt Injection Via Latent Instruction Manifolds
authors: Jiahao Chen, Rui Yin, Xinfeng Li, Qianli Ma, Tianyu Du, Zhihui Fu, Jun Wang, Zhaoxiang Wang, Shouling Ji
abstract: ArXiv:2608.22248v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have been integrated into complex ecosystems (e.g., Code Agents), while Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) attacks have emerged as critical barriers to their safe deployment. Attackers exploit LLMs' indistinguishability between "instructions" and "data" to manipulate LLMs via maliciously injected instructions. Existing defenses, however, face an intractable safety-utility trade-off: most guardrails either incur high latency or suffer from severe over-refusal. In this paper, we first demonstrate that LLMs can separate instruction from data intrinsically with both theoretical and empirical evidence. Inspired by this insight, we propose AEGIS (Adaptive Ensemble Guard for Injection Shielding). AEGIS extracts instruction-sensitive projectors to identify malicious instructions and leverages a Unified Multi-Layer Consensus mechanism that aggregates topologically distinct signals across the network depth. Empirical evaluations show that AEGIS achieves remarkable detection performance against both heuristic and optimization-based attacks compared to baselines, highlighting its potential to mitigate IPI. Code is available at [URL].
tldr: AEGIS is a defense against indirect prompt injection attacks on LLMs, using latent instruction manifolds to distinguish instructions from data, achieving high detection performance without over-refusal.
motivation: LLMs are vulnerable to indirect prompt injection because they cannot reliably separate instructions from data, and existing defenses suffer from high latency or over-refusal, creating a safety-utility trade-off.
method: AEGIS extracts instruction-sensitive projectors and uses a Unified Multi-Layer Consensus mechanism to aggregate topologically distinct signals across network depth to identify malicious instructions.
result: Empirical evaluations show AEGIS achieves remarkable detection performance against both heuristic and optimization-based attacks compared to baselines.
conclusion: AEGIS demonstrates a practical defense against indirect prompt injection, enhancing LLM safety without compromising utility.

title: Secure Wireless Information Transfer And Energy Harvesting In HAPS-Based Network
authors: Khaled Humadi, Gunes Karabulut-Kurt, Wessam Ajib, Wei-Ping Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.22495v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-altitude platform station (HAPS) serves as a promising enabler for wide-area connectivity of low-power wireless devices, particularly in remote and underserved regions. However, the strong line-of-sight characteristics of HAPS links increase the risk of eavesdropping, while the limited energy budget of ground devices remains a major operational constraint. In this work, we propose a secure wireless information and energy harvesting framework for HAPS-based networks in the presence of spatially distributed eavesdroppers. The proposed system integrates friendly jamming and power transfer nodes equipped with null-steering capability antennas, such that they not only degrade the reception quality at eavesdroppers but also act as additional radio-frequency energy sources for legitimate users. A time-switching wireless information and power transfer architecture is adopted at the user side. Under this framework, we derive tractable expressions for the joint rate-energy coverage and the average secrecy rate using stochastic geometry tools. Numerical and Monte Carlo results validate the developed analysis and reveal key design trade-offs among the time allocation factor, null-steering-zone radius around each user, and jammer transmit power. In particular, the results show that properly coordinated null-steering jamming can simultaneously support secure communication and adequate wireless power transfer, while an appropriate choice of system parameters, such as time allocation factor and jamming power, is required to balance harvested energy, communication reliability, and secrecy performance.
tldr: The paper proposes a secure wireless information and energy harvesting framework for HAPS-based networks using friendly jamming and power transfer, with tractable analysis via stochastic geometry.
motivation: HAPS links are susceptible to eavesdropping and ground devices have limited energy, motivating a joint security and energy harvesting solution.
method: The framework integrates null-steering jamming and power transfer nodes, adopts time-switching wireless information and power transfer, and derives joint rate-energy coverage and average secrecy rate using stochastic geometry.
result: Numerical results show that coordinated null-steering jamming can support both secure communication and wireless power transfer, with trade-offs among time allocation, null-steering zone, and jamming power.
conclusion: Proper parameter selection balances harvested energy, communication reliability, and secrecy performance.

title: Femtosecond Laser Induced Metallization In Silicon Via Photon Momentum Mediated Band Transition
authors: Ehatasham Haque, Sunjana Tarannum, Jannatul Shahrin Shoshi, Mahdy Rahman Chowdhury
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21527v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Silicon-based technology has been at the forefront of electronic and photonic research since the dawn of the electronic revolution. However, silicon is fundamentally an indirect-bandgap semiconductor: the conduction band minimum and valence band maximum occur at different points in momentum space, so optical transitions require phonon assistance to conserve crystal momentum. This three-body electron-photon-phonon interaction renders silicon an inefficient material for light-absorbing applications such as solar cells and optoelectronic devices. In this work, we build on an established nanoscale photon-momentum confinement mechanism, which broadens the photon momentum distribution and enables phonon-free absorption in silicon, by subsequently applying a high-intensity femtosecond pulsed excitation that injects hot carriers beyond the Mott density, collapsing the bandgap and inducing a reversible semiconductor-to-metal transition. While nanoscale photon-momentum confinement itself has been previously established, the central contribution of this work is this subsequent, carrier density-driven stage, which drives the momentum-enhanced region into a reversible transient metallic phase. Our simulations report highly negative permittivity, enhanced optical power absorption, a large absorption coefficient, and low skin depth, with carrier densities reaching a notable value, far exceeding the Mott threshold. We have shown carrier driven metallization with stable operation below melting threshold of silicon. These results establish a general mechanism for dynamically inducing metallic states in silicon, offering a potential pathway toward monolithically integrated active photonic components and dynamically reconfigurable electro-optical devices within conventional CMOS platforms.
tldr: This paper simulates femtosecond laser-induced reversible metallization in silicon via photon momentum confinement and hot carrier injection, proposing a mechanism for active photonic components in CMOS platforms.
motivation: Silicon's indirect bandgap limits its optical efficiency; the authors aim to overcome this by inducing a transient metallic phase using high-intensity laser pulses, enabling potential integrated photonic devices.
method: The study builds on established nanoscale photon-momentum confinement, then applies high-intensity femtosecond pulsed excitation to inject hot carriers beyond the Mott density, collapsing the bandgap and driving a reversible metal transition, validated via simulations.
result: Simulations show highly negative permittivity, enhanced optical absorption, large absorption coefficients, and low skin depth, with carrier densities far exceeding the Mott threshold and stable operation below melting threshold.
conclusion: The results establish a general mechanism for dynamically inducing metallic states in silicon, offering potential for monolithically integrated reconfigurable electro-optical devices in CMOS.

title: Finite-term Recurrences In A Generalized Bochner--Krall Family
authors: L. M. Anguas, D. Barrios Rolan\'ia, B. Shapiro, M. Tater
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21802v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify the differential operators \(T=z^j\partial_z^j+z^m\partial_z^\ell\), where \(0\le m<\ell\) and \(1\le j<\ell\), whose monic eigenpolynomials satisfy a finite-term recurrence relation. Writing \(k=\ell-m\), such a recurrence exists if and only if \(j=1\) and \(k\mid\ell\). In that case we determine all recurrence coefficients in closed form and prove that the associated difference operator has order \(\ell\). We also give an explicit factorization showing that every admissible operator is of Type~(2) in Conjecture~1.10 of Horozov--Shapiro--Tater; the equality of the differential and difference orders is the conclusion predicted by their Conjecture~1.9.
tldr: This paper classifies differential operators with finite-term recurrence relations for eigenpolynomials in a generalized Bochner-Krall family, confirming conjectures by Horozov, Shapiro, and Tater.
motivation: To understand when polynomials satisfying certain differential equations admit finite-term recurrence relations, and to verify open conjectures in the theory of orthogonal polynomials.
method: The authors analyze differential operators of the form T = z^j ∂^j + z^m ∂^ℓ, derive algebraic conditions for existence of monic eigenpolynomials with finite-term recurrences, and compute explicit coefficients and operator orders.
result: They prove that finite-term recurrences exist iff j=1 and k divides ℓ, determine all recurrence coefficients in closed form, show the associated difference operator has order ℓ, and provide an explicit factorization for all admissible operators, confirming the conjectured equality of differential and difference orders.
conclusion: The paper provides a complete classification and explicit constructions, thereby resolving the conjectures for this family of operators.

title: Asymptotic Numerical Ranges And Invariant Subspaces Of Operators
authors: Bangyuan Yang Youqing Ji

We define the asymptotic numerical range and the asymptotic numerical radius of [MATH], respectively, by [MATH] and [MATH]. tldr: This paper studies asymptotic numerical ranges and radii for bounded linear operators, proving results about invariant subspaces and spectral radius inequalities.
motivation: The motivation is to understand the asymptotic behavior of numerical ranges and their relation to invariant subspaces in operator theory.
method: The authors define asymptotic numerical range and radius via cluster points of sequences of operator iterates, and analyze their properties using local spectral radius and weak operator topology.
result: They show that under certain conditions, nontrivial hyperinvariant and invariant subspaces exist, and establish inequalities involving the spectral radius, with additional results for hyponormal operators and connectivity of the asymptotic numerical range.
conclusion: The paper advances pure operator theory, but it is unrelated to the specified research directions in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: The Complexity Landscape Of Robust (integer) Linear Programming
authors: Michael Poss, Jannis Kurtz, Marc Goerigk, Dorothee Henke
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the computational complexity of the decision versions of three classic robust optimization problems: static robust optimization, two-stage (adjustable) robust optimization, and [MATH]-adaptability. We consider that the feasibility, uncertainty, and recourse sets are polyhedra or integer-programming-representable sets, the uncertainty is decision-independent or decision-dependent, and the feasible regions are bounded or unbounded. While these problems are well-established in the current literature, we give a systematic classification that places the resulting problems in [MATH], [MATH], [MATH], and higher levels of the polynomial hierarchy ([MATH] and [MATH]), and, once decision-dependent uncertainty introduces quadratic constraints, in the existential theory of the reals and its hierarchy ([MATH], [MATH], and [MATH]) or among the undecidable problems. Beyond hardness reductions, we pay particular attention to membership proofs, establishing polynomial-size certificates even though the sets considered generally contain vectors of exponential encoding length. As a by-product, we give an alternative proof that bilevel linear optimization lies in [MATH], exploiting its connection to decision-dependent robust optimization. For [MATH]-adaptability, we relate the problem to its static and two-stage counterparts, showing that hardness grows monotonically with [MATH] and that, for fully discrete decision-dependent instances, [MATH]-adaptability reduces back to the static problem.
tldr: This paper systematically classifies the computational complexity of decision versions of static, two-stage, and K-adaptability robust linear programming problems, positioning them within the polynomial hierarchy and beyond.
motivation: The computational complexity of robust optimization problems is not well understood, particularly when considering different types of sets and decision-dependent uncertainty.
method: The authors provide a systematic classification using hardness reductions and membership proofs, placing problems in complexity classes such as Σ, Π, and higher levels of the polynomial hierarchy, and also in the existential theory of reals and undecidable problems.
result: They establish polynomial-size certificates for membership and show that hardness grows monotonically with K for K-adaptability, with fully discrete decision-dependent instances reducing to the static problem.
conclusion: The paper provides a comprehensive complexity landscape for robust linear programming variants, clarifying the computational boundaries of these optimization problems.

title: A Diffusion Time-changed Stochastic Sis Epidemic Model: Well-posedness, Long-time Behavior, And Numerical Approximation
authors: Xiaotong Li, Huaqian Zhou, Ruchun Zuo
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose and analyze a diffusion time-changed susceptible-infected-susceptible (SIS) epidemic model driven by time-changed Brownian motion. We prove that the proposed model admits a unique global positive solution for any initial value in [MATH]. The extinction and persistence of the disease are then investigated. To approximate the diffusion time-changed SIS model, we construct a positivity-preserving logarithmic Euler-Maruyama (LEM) method. Assuming that the time-changed is given by the inverse of a standard [MATH]-stable subordinator with [MATH], we prove that the numerical solution converges strongly to the exact solution with order [MATH]. Finally, numerical experiments are provided to confirm the predicted convergence rates and illustrate the positivity-preserving property of the proposed method.
tldr: Proposes and analyzes a time-changed stochastic SIS epidemic model, proving well-posedness, studying disease extinction/persistence, and constructing a numerical approximation method.
motivation: To model epidemic dynamics with time-changed stochasticity, capturing non-standard temporal fluctuations in disease spread.
method: Uses time-changed Brownian motion, establishes existence and uniqueness of global positive solutions, analyzes extinction and persistence conditions, and develops a logarithmic Euler-Maruyama scheme.
result: Proves strong convergence of the numerical method under a stable subordinator time-change, with numerical experiments confirming theoretical rates and positivity preservation.
conclusion: The proposed model and numerical method are valid for stochastic epidemic modeling, offering tools for analyzing disease behavior under time-changed randomness.

title: Hautus Criteria For Exact Controllability And Stabilizability Of Discrete-time Backward-structured Stochastic Linear Systems
authors: Xurun Zuo
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies exact controllability and L2-stabilizability of discrete-time backward-structured stochastic linear systems. For each prescribed finite horizon, equivalent characterizations of exact controllability are established in terms of the controllability Gramian, a Kalman-type rank condition, and the reachable subspace. Exact null controllability without a prescribed horizon is then characterized by a finite-dimensional rank condition, and a Hautus-type criterion is derived using positive semidefinite eigenmatrices of a positive operator. For L2-stabilizability, we establish a stabilizability decomposition and obtain a corresponding Hautus-type spectral criterion. As a byproduct, we show that exact null controllability implies L2-stabilizability. These results provide algebraic and spectral tests for the controllability and stabilizability of the considered systems.
tldr: This paper provides algebraic and spectral tests (Hautus-type criteria) for exact controllability and L2-stabilizability of discrete-time backward-structured stochastic linear systems.
motivation: To characterize controllability and stabilizability of these systems via rank conditions and spectral criteria, which are essential for analysis and design.
method: Derives conditions using the controllability Gramian, Kalman-type rank condition, and reachable subspace; leverages positive semidefinite eigenmatrices and a stabilizability decomposition.
result: Establishes equivalences and Hautus-type criteria, and shows exact null controllability implies L2-stabilizability.
conclusion: Provides new algebraic and spectral tests for controllability and stabilizability, advancing control theory for stochastic linear systems.

title: Topological Centralizers Of Perturbations Of Ergodic Toral Automorphisms With Two Dimensional Center
authors: Boris Petkovi\'c
abstract: ArXiv:2608.22106v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be an ergodic linear automorphism of the torus [MATH] whose center space has dimension two. We prove a dichotomy result that for every [MATH], where [MATH] is the [MATH] neighborhood of [MATH] inside volume preserving diffeomorphisms on [MATH], exactly one of two alternatives holds. Either [MATH] has the accessibility property, or [MATH] is topologically conjugate to [MATH] by a homeomorphism homotopic to the identity which simultaneously conjugates every homeomorphism commuting with [MATH] to an affine automorphism of the torus. No irreducibility of the characteristic polynomial of [MATH] is assumed. The alternatives exclude each other because a partially hyperbolic diffeomorphism topologically conjugate to [MATH] is never accessible, so within [MATH] the failure of accessibility is equivalent to topological conjugacy to [MATH]. In the second case the centralizer of [MATH] in the group of homeomorphisms of the torus is isomorphic to the group of affine transformations commuting with [MATH]. When the characteristic polynomial of [MATH] is irreducible we show that this group is a finite extension of the unit group of an order in the number field generated by an eigenvalue of [MATH], hence virtually free abelian of rank [MATH]. The characteristic polynomial is allowed to be reducible, in which case the same description holds with the linear parts ranging over the centralizer of [MATH] in [MATH]. Our method uses an elementary density property of the projection of the lattice to the center space, which replaces irreducibility and which we establish for every ergodic automorphism with no restriction on the dimension of the center space.
tldr: This paper proves a dichotomy for perturbations of ergodic toral automorphisms with two-dimensional center, showing either accessibility or topological conjugacy to the linear automorphism, and characterizes the centralizer in the latter case.
motivation: To understand the structure of centralizers for partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms on tori and the role of accessibility, generalizing previous results without irreducibility assumptions.
method: Uses an elementary density property of the projection of the lattice to the center space, which replaces irreducibility assumptions for ergodic automorphisms.
result: For every volume-preserving perturbation in a C^1 neighborhood, either the diffeomorphism has the accessibility property or it is topologically conjugate to the linear automorphism by a homeomorphism homotopic to the identity, simultaneously conjugating all commuting homeomorphisms to affine automorphisms.
conclusion: The dichotomy is established without requiring irreducibility of the characteristic polynomial, and the centralizer is characterized as an extension of a unit group when irreducible, or more generally with linear parts ranging over the centralizer of the linear map.

title: A Posteriori Error Estimates For The Two-step Explicit Exponential Adams Method For Parabolic Equations
authors: Wansheng Wang Xianfa Hu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.22162v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we derive optimal order a posteriori error estimates for the variable step-size explicit two-step exponential Adams (E-Adams2) method for parabolic problems. We begin by introducing an E-Adams2 approximation, deffned by the piecewise linear approximate solutions, which leads to suboptimal error estimates. To recover optimal order error estimates, we introducean appropriate reconstruction of the approximation with the second order residual for the explicit E-Adams2 method, which plays key roles in deriving optimal order a posteriori error estimates for the proposed explicit method for linear and semilinear parabolic equations. Various numerical experiments are carried out to verify the correct convergence rates of the a posteriori quantities, and the high efffciency of the adaptive algorithm.
tldr: This paper derives optimal order a posteriori error estimates for the variable step-size explicit two-step exponential Adams method for parabolic equations.
motivation: To ensure efficient adaptive algorithms for parabolic problems, reliable error estimates are needed.
method: Uses piecewise linear approximations and a reconstruction with second-order residual to obtain optimal order a posteriori error estimates.
result: Achieves optimal order a posteriori error estimates and verifies convergence rates via numerical experiments.
conclusion: The proposed E-Adams2 method with adaptive algorithm is efficient and reliable.

title: Sharp Cfl Stability And Temporal-dispersion Optimization Of Symmetric Splitting Schemes For Time-domain Maxwell Equations
authors: Hui Duan, Hongliang Li, Lunzhong Guo
abstract: ArXiv:2608.22315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze coefficient design in a one-parameter family of explicit palindromic electric--magnetic splittings for the time-domain Maxwell equations. After fourth-order staggered spatial discretization, the Fourier amplification matrix depends on the single scalar [MATH]. We prove that [MATH] is the unique real coefficient maximizing the spectral CFL interval, with threshold [MATH]. We then identify a real-coefficient obstruction to higher phase accuracy: cancellation of the leading temporal phase defect requires [MATH], whereas every real member satisfies [MATH]. The resulting complex-conjugate coefficients give fourth-order temporal phase accuracy for each fixed semidiscrete Fourier mode and have threshold [MATH], while the complete field update remains globally second order in time. For real Maxwell data, the physical output is the real projection of the complex trajectory; this projection is branch independent and preserves the second-order error bound. We further give an exactly equivalent doubled real-arithmetic realization, which clarifies the role of the auxiliary imaginary component without changing the numerical method. A semidiscrete convergence result and numerical experiments confirm the distinction between stability optimization and phase optimization.
tldr: This paper analyzes coefficient design in symmetric splitting schemes for time-domain Maxwell equations, proving stability bounds and optimizes temporal dispersion with complex coefficients.
motivation: To improve numerical methods for Maxwell equations by optimizing stability and phase accuracy.
method: They consider a one-parameter family of splitting schemes, analyze the Fourier amplification matrix, and derive conditions for stability and phase accuracy.
result: They prove a unique real coefficient maximizes spectral CFL interval, but complex coefficients improve phase accuracy, with global second-order accuracy.
conclusion: Stability and phase optimization cannot be simultaneously achieved with real coefficients, but complex coefficients give better phase accuracy.

title: Privacy Preserving Semantic Communications In Wireless Edge Networks With Vision Language Models
authors: Haoran Chang, Mingzhe Chen, Qianqian Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21773v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Semantic communication has emerged as a promising paradigm for next-generation wireless systems by transmitting high-level semantic features rather than raw bits. However, collaborative devices and multimodal transmission increase privacy risks because sensitive information may leak through inter-device semantic fusion and cross-modal representations. To address this issue, we propose a privacy-preserving semantic communication framework for wireless edge networks. Leveraging a vision-language model (VLM), the framework extracts textual semantics from images and identifies privacy-sensitive entities using a privacy database maintained only at the edge server. Before image transmission, each device removes the identified private regions while preserving useful semantic content. The server then reconstructs the removed regions from the received masked images using textual embeddings and VLM-based semantic priors. To protect textual information, we design an encrypted semantic-channel transceiver using physical-layer keys generated from reciprocal wireless channels, without pre-shared keys. We also introduce a semantic information bottleneck to suppress redundant information across multiple devices. The framework is evaluated against a strong model-aware adversary that can intercept wireless transmissions and access edge-device model parameters but not server-side data. Simulation results show that the proposed method reduces privacy leakage by more than 50% compared with a semantic communication scheme without privacy protection, while the authorized server achieves a 48% improvement in perceptual reconstruction quality over the adversary. The estimated mutual information between transmitted representations approaches 0 bit, indicating effective suppression of cross-device semantic redundancy.
tldr: Proposes a privacy-preserving semantic communication framework for wireless edge networks using vision-language models to mask sensitive regions and physical-layer keys for encryption.
motivation: Collaborative devices and multimodal transmission increase privacy risks in semantic communication; need to protect sensitive information during semantic fusion and cross-modal representation.
method: Uses a VLM to identify and remove private image regions, server reconstructs with textual embeddings, and an encrypted semantic-channel transceiver with physical-layer keys; also employs a semantic information bottleneck.
result: Reduces privacy leakage by over 50% and improves reconstruction quality by 48% over adversary, with mutual information near zero.
conclusion: The framework effectively suppresses cross-device semantic redundancy and enhances privacy in wireless edge networks.

title: Breaking The Assumptions: Auditing Input-Side Jailbreak Defenses Against Semantic Attacks
authors: Aaditya Pratap, Harsh Kasyap, Somanath Tripathy
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21895v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Locally deployed Large Language Models (LLMs) via inference engines such as Ollama run without the moderation and abuse detection present in API-served models. Therefore, the safety of LLMs depends on the defense mechanisms used, and their effectiveness depends on the assumptions on which they were designed. This paper does an audit of defense mechanisms under jailbreak attacks on locally deployed models. Some defenses provide formal guarantees (SmoothLLM, Erase-and-Check, Sequential Monitors), while others rely on empirical detection results (Semantic Smoothing, Self-Denoised Smoothing, Perplexity Filtering). Instead of merely observing that defenses fail, we trace each failure back to the specific assumption: for every defense, we extract the condition it relies on, derive the empirical pattern a violation should produce, and test that prediction on six open-weight models (14B to 35B parameters) with a corpus of 100 jailbreak prompts taken from more than 40 public sources, totalling 13,800 evaluation records.
tldr: This paper audits input-side jailbreak defenses for locally deployed LLMs by tracing failures to violated assumptions, tested on six open-weight models with 100 jailbreak prompts.
motivation: Locally deployed LLMs lack moderation and abuse detection, making safety dependent on defense mechanisms whose effectiveness relies on specific assumptions that may not hold under semantic attacks.
method: The authors extract the assumption each defense relies on, derive empirical patterns a violation would produce, and test these predictions on six open-weight models with a corpus of 100 jailbreak prompts from 40+ sources, totaling 13,800 evaluation records.
result: The audit reveals that defenses fail due to assumption violations, and each failure is traced back to the specific assumption that was broken.
conclusion: The paper highlights that current input-side jailbreak defenses are vulnerable to semantic attacks, emphasizing the need for defense mechanisms that do not rely on easily violated assumptions.

title: SkillBloat: Token Amplification Attacks Via Skill Injection In Llm Coding Agents
authors: Jingbang Chen Yuanjin Zheng
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21929v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent skills extend coding agents with task-specific instructions, scripts, and resources, but they also create a trusted instruction channel that can be abused beyond conventional security attacks. This paper studies token amplification through skill injection: an economic resource-abuse threat in which a malicious skill causes an agent to consume substantially more tokens than needed for normal task execution. We present SkillBloat, a two-phase framework that first screens a library of diverse attack-type conditions across multiple amplification mechanisms and then refines the strongest candidate through LLM-guided full-document skill rewriting. Evaluated on a real-world skill benchmark, SkillBloat achieves 5.4184x-10.1455x average best amplification across multiple coding-agent target configurations. An ablation shows that the second-stage refinement loop consistently improves average best amplification over Phase 1 attack-type screening alone, demonstrating that iterative optimization provides additional benefit beyond initial attack-type selection. These results show that skill ecosystems expose a practical resource-amplification attack surface that is orthogonal to existing security-oriented skill poisoning.
tldr: This paper introduces SkillBloat, a framework to amplify token consumption in LLM coding agents via malicious skill injection.
motivation: Skill ecosystems in coding agents create a trusted instruction channel that can be abused to cause excessive token usage, leading to economic resource abuse.
method: SkillBloat uses a two-phase approach: first screening diverse attack-type conditions, then refining the best candidate with LLM-guided full-document skill rewriting.
result: It achieves 5.4184x-10.1455x average best amplification on a real-world skill benchmark, and ablation shows the refinement loop improves amplification.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a practical resource-amplification attack surface orthogonal to existing security-oriented skill poisoning.

title: Autonomous Cyber Defense: Real-Time Attack Detection And Mitigation In Software-Defined Networks Using Machine Learning
authors: Alexandre Amaral, Fernando Moro, Ana Malheiro
abstract: ArXiv:2608.22075v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adversaries now move faster than manual response processes can absorb. The average eCrime breakout time, that is, the interval between initial access and the first lateral movement to another host, fell to 29 minutes in 2025, a 65\% increase in speed over the previous year; the fastest observed breakout took 27 seconds, and in one intrusion data exfiltration began within four minutes of initial access. This work presents a machine learning based system that monitors network traffic in real time, diagnoses attacks, and automatically applies countermeasures in software-defined networks, so that detection and response no longer depend on human intervention. The system comprises two modules: (NDC), which collects IP flows, preprocesses and aggregates them to build the training dataset, and (IPS), which automates the modeling, training, and evaluation of different algorithms and triggers blocking actions on the SDN controller. A case study with a denial of service attack, shows the attack being detected and blocked in 21 seconds without human intervention, a response time compatible with the window imposed by current breakout times.
tldr: This paper presents a machine learning-based system for autonomous cyber defense in software-defined networks, detecting and mitigating attacks without human intervention.
motivation: The need for faster response to cyber attacks, as manual response times are insufficient compared to attack speeds.
method: It uses two modules: NDC for data collection and preprocessing, and IPS for model training, evaluation, and automated blocking actions via the SDN controller.
result: In a case study with a DoS attack, the system detected and blocked it in 21 seconds without human intervention.
conclusion: The system demonstrates that autonomous detection and response can meet the required time windows, reducing dependence on human intervention.

title: Neighbor-embedded Graph Neural Network-based Crowd Delivery Traffic Management In Smart City
authors: Kishu Gupta, Deepika Saxena, Ashutosh Kumar Singh, Chung-Nan Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2608.22555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The significant upsurge in vehicle traffic presents a considerable challenge in the pursuit of smart mobilization and transportation (SMT) worldwide. Current approaches primarily focus on vehicular traffic management through congestion prediction but fall short in addressing essential objectives such as traffic reduction and appropriate vehicle selection to alleviate congestion in smart cities ([MATH]). To address these concerns, this work introduces a novel (NeCDM) Model, comprising two key components: the Traffic Congestion Prediction Unit (TCPu) and the Traffic Observation and Management Unit (TOMu). The TCPu utilizes Graph Neural Network (GNN) optimization to accurately predict traffic flow levels at various delivery stations within [MATH] ecosystems. Additionally, the TOMu facilitates the intelligent selection of the most suitable delivery vehicles for fulfilling crowd delivery requests ([MATH]). This work emphasizes the potential of crowd delivery as a feasible solution for achieving SMT goals while adhering to smart city parameters ([MATH]s), such as reduced carbon emissions, shorter travel times, and minimized travel distances. The proposed model achieves notable improvements in computational efficiency, including reductions of up to 4.03\% in L1 loss ([MATH]), 16.66\% in L2 loss ([MATH]), and 7.64\% in computation time.
tldr: Proposes a graph neural network-based model for traffic congestion prediction and vehicle selection in smart city crowd delivery systems.
motivation: Addresses limitations of existing traffic management approaches that focus only on congestion prediction without optimizing vehicle selection for crowd delivery to meet smart city goals.
method: Introduces the NeCDM model with a Traffic Congestion Prediction Unit (TCPu) using GNN optimization and a Traffic Observation and Management Unit (TOMu) for intelligent vehicle selection.
result: Achieves reductions of up to 4.03% in L1 loss, 16.66% in L2 loss, and 7.64% in computation time.
conclusion: Demonstrates the potential of crowd delivery combined with GNN-based prediction and management to enhance smart mobility and reduce environmental impact.

title: Average-Radius List-Decodability Of Random Linear Codes
authors: Venkatesan Guruswami, Shilun Li, Mihir Singhal
abstract: ArXiv:2608.22663v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for every prime power [MATH] and every [MATH], a random [MATH]-linear code of rate [MATH] is [MATH]-average-radius list-decodable with probability at least [MATH], i.e., for every center [MATH], the [MATH] codewords closest to [MATH] have average fractional Hamming distance at least [MATH] from [MATH]. This extends a similar result for (standard) list-decoding due to Guruswami, Hstad, and Kopparty (2010) to the stronger average-radius guarantee, with the same [MATH] list size. For average-radius list-decoding, such a result was previously known only for binary linear codes (Guruswami, Li, Mosheiff, Resch, Silas, and Wootters, 2021) and for general (non-linear) random codes over arbitrary alphabets (Elias, 1991).
tldr: The paper proves that random linear codes over a finite field are average-radius list-decodable with high probability, extending previous results on standard list-decoding.
motivation: The work aims to strengthen known results about list-decodability of random linear codes by considering the average-radius guarantee, which is stronger than the usual list-decoding radius.
method: The authors use probabilistic arguments and combinatorial techniques to show that for any given center, the codewords nearest to it have average Hamming distance at least a certain threshold.
result: They prove that for every prime power q and every rate R, a random q-ary linear code of rate R is average-radius list-decodable with high probability, with the same list size as the standard list-decoding result.
conclusion: This extends prior results to the average-radius setting and to all finite fields, generalizing known binary and non-linear cases.
